📄 Complete Details & Notification

The Railway Recruitment Board (RRB) is expected to release the RRB Group D Result 2026 in the 4th week of June 2026 at the official website rrbcdg.gov.in, following the disposal of the Telangana High Court case that had earlier put a hold on the result. Over 1.08 crore candidates who appeared for the Computer Based Test (CBT) under CEN 08/2024 for 32,438 Level 1 vacancies can check their merit list, scorecard, and zone-wise cut off marks once the result is declared. This article covers everything candidates need to know the latest court case update, how to check the result, scorecard details, cut off expectations, and the next stage of selection.

RRB Group D Result 2026 - Latest Update

This section explains the most recent development in the RRB Group D result timeline, including the court case status and the revised expected release date.

The Telangana High Court has disposed of the petition concerning Course Completed Act Apprentice (CCAA) weightage marks on 16th June 2026, removing the stay that had earlier delayed the result. With the legal hurdle cleared, the Railway Recruitment Board is now expected to declare the RRB Group D Result 2026 in the 4th week of June 2026, along with the scorecard, merit list, and cut off marks. As a precautionary step, the court has directed RRB to keep 15 vacancies reserved until final disposal of the main writ petition, while the remaining 32,423 posts will be filled through the regular recruitment process. RRB has also opened an application modification window for CCAA candidates from 17th June to 23rd June 2026, allowing them to update NCVT certificate details and marks before the result is finalised.

RRB Group D Result 2026 Overview

This section gives a quick snapshot of the exam, vacancies, and important result-related dates for CEN 08/2024 in one place.

Particulars Details
Exam Name RRB Group D
Conducting Body Railway Recruitment Board (RRB)

Post Level Level 1 (7th CPC Pay Matrix)
Total Vacancies 32,438
Exam Dates 27th November 2025 to 10th February 2026
Answer Key Released 17th February 2026
CCAA Application Modification Window 17th June to 23rd June 2026
Result Date 4th week of June 2026 (Expected)
Scorecard Release 4th week of June 2026 (Expected)
Total Candidates Appeared 10,822,423
Selection Process CBT, PET, Document Verification, Medical Test
Official Website rrbcdg.gov.in and respective zonal RRB websites

Why Was the RRB Group D Result Delayed?

This section explains the background of the court case that caused the delay in declaring the result.

The result was delayed due to a case filed in the Telangana High Court relating to the weightage given to Course Completed Act Apprentice (CCAA) candidates in the final merit list. The dispute arose after a 2022 policy change by the Skill Development Ministry altered the earlier exemption available to apprenticeship candidates, prompting petitioners to demand restoration of the older selection system. Since the outcome could affect zone-wise rankings and cut off marks, RRB suspended further processing of the result until the court's verdict. With the case now disposed of, the court has directed the Directorate General of Training (DGT) to examine the representations on the 2022 policy change, and has instructed Railway authorities to conduct proper scrutiny of CCAA candidates during document verification.

How to Check RRB Group D Result 2026 at rrbcdg.gov.in

This section lists the step-by-step process candidates need to follow once the result link is activated.

  1. Visit the official website of your respective regional RRB (for example, rrbcdg.gov.in).
  2. Look for the result link titled "CEN-RRB-08/2024 (Pay Level-1 Posts): CBT Result & Score Card."
  3. Click on the relevant zone-wise result/merit list link.
  4. Download the result PDF that appears on the screen.
  5. Use Ctrl + F to search for your registration number or roll number in the PDF.
  6. Log in with your registration number and date of birth to view your individual scorecard.
  7. Download and print the result for future reference.

RRB Group D Scorecard 2026: What It Will Contain

This section explains where the scorecard will be available and what details candidates should verify on it.

The RRB Group D Scorecard 2026 will be released along with the result on the candidate login portal at rrb.digialm.com. Candidates must check every detail on the scorecard carefully to avoid discrepancies later. The scorecard will typically include:

  • Candidate's Name
  • Registration Number
  • Date of Birth and Gender
  • Roll Number
  • Father's/Mother's Name
  • Category and Quota Sub-Category (if applicable)
  • Total Exam Marks and Marks Scored
  • Total Cut-Off Score
  • RRB Region/Zone Venue

RRB Group D Merit List 2026: Zone-Wise Release

This section explains how the merit list will be structured and how candidates can locate their result within it.

The RRB Group D Merit List 2026 will be released separately for each of the RRB's 21 regional zones in PDF format, containing the roll numbers of shortlisted candidates. Since the list runs into thousands of roll numbers, candidates are advised to use the Ctrl + F search function within the PDF to quickly locate their roll number instead of scrolling manually. The result and merit list will be published on each zone's respective official website, including rrbcdg.gov.in (Chandigarh), rrbmumbai.gov.in, rrbchennai.gov.in, rrbkolkata.gov.in, rrbbpl.nic.in, and other zonal RRB portals.

RRB Group D Cut Off 2026: What to Expect

This section explains how the cut off marks will be determined and where they will be published.

The RRB Group D Cut Off 2026 will be released zone-wise and category-wise (UR, OBC, SC, ST, EWS) along with the result and merit list. Since the CBT was conducted across multiple shifts over several months, RRB applies an equi-percentile normalisation method to ensure fairness raw marks in each shift are converted to a percentile scale, and this normalised score (not the raw score) is used to prepare the final merit list. As per the official notification, the minimum qualifying marks are:

Category Minimum Qualifying Marks
UR / EWS 40%
OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) / SC 30%
ST 25%

Candidates must clear both the category-wise qualifying marks and the overall zone cut off to be considered for the Physical Efficiency Test (PET).

What Happens After the RRB Group D Result 2026?

This section explains the next stages in the selection process that follow the result declaration.

Candidates who qualify in the CBT will be shortlisted for the Physical Efficiency Test (PET), which is qualifying in nature meaning candidates only need to clear it, and PET marks are not added to the final merit. Those who clear the PET will then proceed to Document Verification, where original certificates, identity proof, and category certificates (including NCVT/CCAA documents, given the recent court directions) must be presented. CCAA candidates should particularly note that RRB will conduct proper scrutiny and eligibility verification of their certificates during this stage, as directed by the Telangana High Court.

The SSC Delhi Police Constable Result 2026 has been officially released by the Staff Selection Commission (SSC) on 19th June 2026 at ssc.gov.in. Candidates who appeared for the Computer-Based Examination (CBE) held from 18th December 2025 to 6th January 2026 can now check whether they have been shortlisted for the next stage the Physical Endurance Test (PET) and Physical Measurement Test (PMT). A total of 66,076 candidates have been shortlisted out of 27,25,888 applicants who competed for 7,201 posts. Read on for category-wise cut offs, direct PDF download links, scorecard access steps, and everything you need to know about what comes next.

How to Download SSC Delhi Police Constable Result 2026

Checking the result is a simple process. Follow the step-by-step instructions below to download the shortlisted candidates' PDF from the official SSC website without any confusion.

SSC Delhi Police Constable Cut Off 2026 - Category-Wise

The SSC has released the official category-wise cut off marks along with the result. The cut off is the minimum score a candidate must have secured in the CBE to be shortlisted for the PET and PMT round. Candidates scoring at or above the cut off in their respective categories have been called for the physical tests.

How to Download SSC Delhi Police Constable Scorecard 2026

Apart from the result PDF, SSC also provides an individual scorecard for all candidates who appeared in the CBE. The scorecard mentions section-wise marks in Reasoning, General Knowledge & Current Affairs, Numerical Ability, and Computer Fundamentals, along with the total score. Here is how to access your scorecard:

  1. Go to ssc.gov.in and click on "Candidate Login".

BPSC 70th CCE Final Result 2026: Shraddha Pandey Tops Merit List as 2,027 Candidates Selected

The Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) has officially declared the BPSC 70th Combined Competitive Examination (CCE) Final Result 2026 on June 20, 2026. The result was announced in Patna by BPSC Chairman Ravi Manubhai Parmar, bringing the curtain down on one of the largest and most closely watched recruitment drives in the Commission's history. Out of 2,035 advertised vacancies, 2,027 candidates have been finally selected, while 8 posts reserved for Persons with Disabilities (PwD) remain unfilled due to the unavailability of eligible candidates. Uttar Pradesh's Shraddha Pandey has emerged as the overall topper with 593 marks. Candidates can check their selection status by downloading the final merit list PDF from the official BPSC website.

BPSC 70th CCE 2026 Topper List: Who Scored the Highest Marks?

Many aspirants want to know who led the merit list and by what margin. Shraddha Pandey from Uttar Pradesh secured All-India Rank 1 with 593 marks, narrowly ahead of the second and third rank holders.

Rank Candidate Name Marks Secured
1 Shraddha Pandey 593
2 Shashank Gaurav 592
3 Ayush Bijoy 592

The gap of just one mark between the top three candidates reflects how intensely contested the 70th CCE was, with thousands of aspirants separated by only a handful of marks across the merit list.

How to Check and Download BPSC 70th CCE Final Result 2026 PDF

Once the result is declared, the next logical step for any candidate is locating and verifying their name in the official PDF. Follow these steps to check your BPSC 70th CCE final result without any hassle:

  • Visit the official BPSC website at bpsc.bih.nic.in.
  • Look for the "Latest Updates" or "Results" section on the homepage.
  • Click on the link reading "70th Combined Competitive Examination Final Result."
  • The result PDF will open in a new window.
  • Press Ctrl + F (or Cmd + F on Mac) and type your roll number or name to search.
  • If your details appear in the list, you have been recommended for appointment.
  • Download and save the PDF, or take a printout for future reference.

BPSC 70th CCE 2026: A Look at the Recruitment Journey

The 70th CCE was not a smooth process from start to finish. Understanding the exam's timeline helps explain why this result was so widely anticipated and why it took longer than usual to declare.

Preliminary Exam Controversy and Re-Conduct

The preliminary examination ran into trouble early on after irregularities were reported at the Bapu Examination Complex in Patna, prompting BPSC to cancel the test held at that specific centre. Despite demands from protesting candidates to scrap the entire exam, BPSC re-conducted the affected preliminary test on January 4, 2025, across 22 centres in Patna, while maintaining that the overall process remained transparent and fair.

Mains Examination and Interview Stage

The Mains examination was conducted over multiple days in April 2025 at several centres in Patna, with results announced later that year. Following the Mains result, 5,401 candidates were shortlisted and called for the personal interview round, which was the final stage before the merit list was prepared.

BPSC 70th CCE Final Result 2026: Selection Statistics

The scale of this recruitment cycle makes it one of the biggest in BPSC's history. The numbers below show how the candidate pool narrowed down at each stage of the selection process.

Officials cited the sheer volume of candidates as a key reason behind the extended timeline for completing interviews and finalizing the merit list.

Why Is the BPSC 70th CCE Considered a Landmark Recruitment Drive?

The scale of this exam stands out when compared with recent BPSC cycles, and that context helps explain why the result has drawn so much attention. The 70th CCE offered 2,035 vacancies, making it significantly larger than the two examinations before it. For comparison, the 68th BPSC exam had only 324 vacancies, while the 69th BPSC exam offered 475 vacancies. This jump in vacancy numbers, combined with over 4.8 lakh applications, made the 70th CCE one of the biggest civil services recruitment exercises conducted by the Commission since Independence.

What Happens After the BPSC 70th CCE Final Result 2026?

Clearing the final merit list is not the last step for selected candidates. A few formalities remain before they can officially join their posts.

  • Document Verification and Medical Test: Selected candidates must produce original documents and clear a mandatory medical fitness examination.
  • Department and Service Allocation: Postings are allotted based on merit rank, category, and candidates' service preferences.
  • Appointment Letters: Official appointment letters are issued by the respective administrative departments.
  • Foundation Training: Newly appointed officers undergo mandatory training before taking up their assigned duties.

Mizoram PSC Assistant Grade and UDC Final Result 2026 - Official Merit List Declared on 19th June

The Mizoram Public Service Commission (MPSC) has officially declared the Final Result 2026 for the posts of Assistant Grade and Upper Division Clerk (UDC) under various departments of the Government of Mizoram. The result was published on 19th June 2026 through official notification number NON-TECHNICAL/4/2025-MPSC(PE), issued from the Mizoram New Capital Complex, Khatla, Aizawl. Candidates who appeared in the Combined Competitive Examination held on 9th October 2025 and the Personal Interview conducted between 15th May and 19th June 2026 can now verify their selection status in the official merit list published by the MPSC.

Reserved Panel - Important Information for Candidates

As per Guideline 36(10) of the Mizoram Public Service Commission (Conduct of Examinations) Guidelines 2023, a reserved panel has been maintained alongside the main merit list. Candidates who were not directly recommended but are placed in the reserved panel should note the following key points.

  • The reserved panel is activated only when selected candidates decline the appointment offer, resign before joining, or pass away after the result declaration.
  • Reserved panel candidates will be considered for appointment in the order of their merit and post preferences.
  • The reserved panel is valid for one year from the date of result declaration, i.e., from 19th June 2026 to 19th June 2027.
  • After this one-year period, the reserved panel will lapse and cannot be used to fill vacancies.

How to Check Mizoram PSC Assistant and UDC Final Result 2026 Online

Candidates can access and verify their result in the official MPSC Final Result 2026 PDF by following the step-by-step process below.

  4. Click to open or download the official PDF notification.
  5. Use the Ctrl+F (Find) function to search for your name or roll number within the document.
  6. Note your position on the merit list, your total marks, and your assigned Post Preference Code.

The Arunachal Pradesh Staff Selection Board (APSSB) has released the provisional result for the Special Recruitment Drive written examination held on 14 June 2026, covering the posts of Constable, Fireman, and Special Tiger Guard. The result was officially published on 20 June 2026 and is available as a downloadable PDF on the APSSB website, apssb.nic.in. Candidates who appeared for this exam can check their roll numbers in the released list to know their provisional qualification status.

This article covers everything candidates need to know about the APSSB Provisional Result 2026 including the official download link, background of the recruitment drive, the posts involved, and the likely next steps in the selection process.

What Is the APSSB Provisional Result 2026?

The APSSB Provisional Result 2026 is an official list published by the Arunachal Pradesh Staff Selection Board showing the roll numbers of candidates who appeared in the written examination conducted on 14 June 2026 for the Special Drive Exam for Constable, Fireman, and Special Tiger Guard posts. Being "provisional" means the result is subject to verification candidates' final selection still depends on document verification, physical tests, and other stages of the recruitment process as specified by APSSB.

Direct Link to Download APSSB Provisional Result PDF

Candidates can access the official provisional result through the link below.

Detail Information
Exam Date 14 June 2026 (Sunday)
Result Declared On 20 June 2026
Posts Covered Constable, Fireman, Special Tiger Guard
Conducting Body Arunachal Pradesh Staff Selection Board (APSSB)
Official Website apssb.nic.in

Official PDF Link: APSSB First Provisional Result 2026

Candidates should open this PDF and search their roll number using Ctrl+F (on a desktop) to quickly locate their result status.

Background: What Recruitment Drive Is This Result For?

This section explains the recruitment context behind this exam and result.

This provisional result relates to the APSSB Special Recruitment Drive for Uniformed Services Combined Examination 2026, a large-scale hiring drive announced earlier in 2026 for Group C uniformed posts in Arunachal Pradesh. Key facts about this recruitment drive include:

  • The notification was released for 984 vacancies across uniformed services posts.
  • Posts included Constable (IRBn/Civil Police), Fireman, Constable Band, Constable Bugler, and Special Tiger Guard (under STPF).
  • Online applications were accepted from 23 March 2026 to 20 April 2026.
  • The minimum educational qualification for these posts is generally Class 10 (Matriculation) pass from a recognised board.
  • The written examination, originally scheduled differently, was rescheduled and finally conducted on 14 June 2026.

Posts Covered Under This Result: Constable, Fireman, and Special Tiger Guard

This section briefly explains the three post categories named in this result.

  • Constable: Includes Constable under the Indian Reserve Battalion (IRBn) and Constable Civil Police, responsible for general law-and-order duties within Arunachal Pradesh Police.
  • Fireman: A Group C post under the fire and emergency services department, responsible for firefighting and emergency response duties.
  • Special Tiger Guard (STPF): A post under the Special Tiger Protection Force, tasked with wildlife and tiger reserve protection duties within the state's forest department.

How to Check Your APSSB Provisional Result

This section gives candidates a simple step-by-step method to check their result.

  1. Visit the official APSSB website: apssb.nic.in.
  2. Look for the notice titled "APSSB Spl Drive Exam 14th June Provisional Result."
  3. Click on the link to open the PDF, or use the direct link provided above.
  4. Use the search function (Ctrl+F) to find your roll number within the PDF list.
  5. Download or save the PDF for future reference, since it may be needed at later selection stages.

What Happens After the Provisional Result?

This section outlines the general next stages typically followed in such recruitment drives, based on the official notification.

Since this is a provisional result, candidates whose roll numbers appear are generally expected to proceed to further stages of the selection process as defined in the official notification, which for these posts typically include a Physical Efficiency Test (PET), Physical Standard Test (PST), document verification, and a medical fitness test. Candidates are advised to keep checking the official APSSB website regularly for further notices regarding the schedule and venue of subsequent stages, as these specifics are announced separately by the Board.

How These UPPBPB Results Were Finalized

This section explains the official process the Board followed between the provisional answer key and the final result, which is important context for understanding why some questions were cancelled or answer keys revised.

Both notices follow the same standard procedure used by UPPBPB for written examinations:

  • The provisional answer key was published on 29 May 2026, and candidates were invited to submit online objections regarding any question or answer option.
  • After the objection window closed, the Board examined each objection and either retained, revised, or cancelled the relevant question.
  • Marks allotted to cancelled questions were distributed equally among the remaining questions in the same paper, applying the principle laid down in Writ Petition No. 2669/2009 (M/B), Pawan Kumar Aghari vs. State of U.P. Public Service Commission.
  • Final merit lists were then prepared strictly on the basis of marks scored in the written exam, and selection lists were published as annexures to the result notice.

Both official notices also clarify that while the Board exercises due care while uploading results to its website, it will not be held responsible for any technical error, and no candidate can claim any benefit or right arising from such an error if one is later discovered.

The Indian Coast Guard has released the Stage-III Admit Card for candidates in the Navik GD & Yantrik CGEPT 01/2026 & 02/2026 Batch recruitment drive. The admit card became available from 19 June 2026 and can be downloaded from the official Indian Coast Guard website by logging in with your registered email ID, password, and captcha code. What Is the Coast Guard Navik CGEPT 02/2026 Stage-III Admit Card?

This section explains what the Stage-III admit card is and why it matters for candidates who have already cleared the earlier stages of the CGEPT recruitment process.

The Stage-III Admit Card is issued to candidates who have qualified the written examination and OMR-based assessment for the Navik (General Duty), Navik (Domestic Branch), and Yantrik posts under the CGEPT 01/2026 & 02/2026 Batch. This stage typically involves a detailed document verification round and a medical examination, conducted at INS Chilka. The written examination for this recruitment cycle was held from 19 to 22 September 2025, and candidates who cleared the earlier stages are now required to download this admit card to appear for Stage-III.

Coast Guard Navik CGEPT 02/2026 - Important Dates

This section lists all the key dates related to the CGEPT 01/2026 & 02/2026 Batch recruitment cycle, from the start of online applications to the release of the Stage-III admit card.

Exam City Details Released 04 September 2025

Candidates are advised to keep checking the official Indian Coast Guard website for any further updates regarding their Stage-III admit card or examination schedule.

How to Download Coast Guard Navik & Yantrik Stage-III Admit Card 2026

This section provides a simple step-by-step guide for candidates to log in and download their Stage-III admit card from the official portal.

  1. Visit the official Indian Coast Guard recruitment portal at joinindiancoastguard.cdac.in.
  2. On the homepage, click on the "Candidate Login" option.
  3. Select your Post Name (Navik or Yantrik) and the relevant Batch Number (01/2026 or 02/2026).
  4. Enter your registered Email ID, Password, and the Captcha Code displayed on screen.
  5. Click on the "Login" or "Submit" button.
  6. After logging in, click on the "Stage-III Admit Card" link.
  7. Your admit card will be displayed on the screen.
  8. Download and print the admit card and keep it safe for future reference and for carrying to the examination/document verification venue.

Interview (Current Stage) Offline / In-Person Panel Interview 100 Marks

About the Interview Round

The interview is a panel-based personal interview conducted in English or Hindi. It assesses the candidate's technical or domain knowledge (relevant to the applied stream), communication skills, banking awareness, analytical thinking, and overall personality. The panel typically consists of senior bank officials and external experts.

Important Instructions for BOI Officers Interview 2026

Candidates appearing for the BOI Officers Interview 2026 must follow all official instructions to avoid disqualification. Here are the key guidelines you need to be aware of before attending the interview.

  • Arrive at the interview venue at least 30-45 minutes before the reporting time mentioned on the call letter.
  • Carry the call letter in printed form - digital / mobile copies may not be accepted at the centre.
  • Bring the original valid photo ID along with at least one self-attested photocopy.
  • Dress professionally and formally for the interview. Bank interviews require business/formal attire.
  • Mobile phones and electronic devices may not be allowed inside the interview hall - check venue guidelines.
  • Candidates who have registered as PwBD should carry their valid disability certificate.
  • OBC candidates must carry the most recent Non-Creamy Layer Certificate in the format prescribed by the Government of India.
  • Do not bring unauthorised materials such as study notes, books, or electronic gadgets into the interview room.
  • Candidates shortlisted for interview must ensure their application details match the documents being presented.

Quick Tips to Prepare for BOI Officers Interview 2026

The interview is the final hurdle between you and a confirmed officer position at Bank of India. Here are some practical preparation tips that can help you make a strong impression before the panel.

  • Know your CV thoroughly - Be ready to answer questions on every project, role, and achievement you have mentioned.
  • Brush up on banking fundamentals - Topics like RBI monetary policy, credit risk, NPA norms, Basel III, and MSME lending are commonly discussed.
  • Stay current with financial news - Read The Economic Times or RBI bulletins in the week leading up to your interview.
  • Understand Bank of India's recent performance - Know the bank's key financial indicators, schemes, and latest initiatives.
  • Practice structured answers - Use the STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result) method for experience-based questions.
  • Prepare for stream-specific questions - If you have applied for a credit or specialist stream, expect deep domain knowledge questions.

What Is the Physical Screening Test (PST)?

This section explains the purpose of the PST stage within the overall Constable selection process.

The Physical Screening Test is a qualifying stage in the Haryana Police Constable selection process, conducted after the Physical Measurement Test (PMT), which checks height and chest measurements. The PST assesses the physical fitness and endurance of candidates through a timed running race, and only those who clear this stage move forward in the recruitment process toward the Knowledge Test (written exam), followed by Document Verification and Medical Examination.

Common Issues & Solutions While Downloading City Slip

Issue #1: Unable to Login / Invalid Credentials Error

Solutions:

  • Verify your registration number carefully (no spaces before/after)
  • Check date of birth format if using DOB: DD/MM/YYYY
  • Ensure CAPS LOCK is off while entering details
  • Clear your browser cache and cookies (Ctrl+Shift+Del)
  • Try using a different web browser (Chrome, Firefox, or Edge)
  • Use “Forgot Password” link if needed
  • Check your registered email for confirmation details

Issue #2: City Slip Not Showing / Page Not Loading

Solutions:

  • Verify if city slip is released for your slot
  • Try downloading during non-peak hours (early morning or late night)
  • Disable VPN, proxy, or ad-blocker extensions
  • Check your internet connection stability
  • Try using mobile data instead of WiFi (or vice versa)
  • Use incognito/private browsing mode
  • Update your web browser to the latest version

Issue #3: Error in Details Displayed on City Slip

Solutions:

  • Contact SSC helpdesk immediately via regional offices
  • Email or call with screenshot and registration details
  • Keep your registration number ready
  • Explain the exact discrepancy in detail
  • Request for correction before exam date

Issue #4: PDF Download Not Working

Solutions:

  • Take a screenshot of the city slip as backup
  • Try “Print to PDF” option (Ctrl+P then save as PDF)
  • Use a different PDF reader (Adobe Acrobat Reader)
  • Check if pop-ups are blocked in browser settings
  • Ensure sufficient storage space on device
  • Try downloading from different device

Issue #5: Captcha Not Visible or Loading

Solutions:

  • Refresh the page (F5 key)
  • Enable JavaScript in browser settings
  • Disable browser extensions temporarily
  • Use a different browser
  • Clear browser cache completely

What is SSC City Intimation Slip 2026?

The SSC City Intimation Slip 2026 is an advance notification document released before the admit card. It provides candidates with essential preliminary information about their examination to help them make necessary travel and accommodation arrangements. The city slip is NOT your admit card but serves as an important reference document.

Key Information Available in City Slip:

  • Allotted exam city and state
  • Scheduled exam date
  • Shift timing (Morning/Afternoon/Evening)

Eligibility Criteria - KSP Armed Police Constable 2026

Before applying for the KSP Constable recruitment 2026, candidates must verify that they meet all the eligibility requirements including educational qualification, age limit, and nationality. Ineligible candidates who apply will be disqualified at any stage of the selection process.

Nationality

The applicant must be an Indian citizen.

Educational Qualification

The minimum educational qualification for KSP Armed Police Constable Recruitment 2026 is PUC (Class 12) or equivalent. Candidates who are currently studying and awaiting results are NOT eligible. All candidates must have passed PUC or hold equivalent marks on or before the last date of application.

  • Class 12 passed from CBSE / SSLC board
  • Class 12 from any other State Government examination board
  • Higher-level education (H.S.C.) conducted by the National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS)
  • Two-year ITI course holders: one language course + one technical subject at the PUC level (distance / regular) in one language and one subject is the minimum

Special Note (GO No. 19 TVA 2019, dated 06.08.2021): Vocational Training Courses (J.O.C.) are treated as equivalent to PUC under the following conditions only:

  • Students awaiting compassionate / same-rotation appointment, or those whose appointment orders are pending - JOC is treated as equivalent to PUC.
  • If PUC or JOC marks are being considered only for competitive exams (not for employment), JOC is treated as the minimum qualification.

Three-year Diploma holders (GO No. 33 TVA 2021, dated 30.09.2021): A 3-year diploma from a technical institution is treated as equivalent to PUC subject to the following:

  • For direct or compassionate recruitment and for higher education, a 3-year technical diploma is treated as PUC equivalent.
  • Students who obtained a 3-year technical diploma before 2015 must additionally pass the Kannada language exam conducted by KPSC alongside the departmental test.

Important (Note-b): As per GO No. 43 / 2020 (dated 5.3.2021) and GO No. 102 / 2022 (dated 24.03.2025), candidates appearing for the KSP recruitment exam must have passed the Kannada language test conducted by SSLC/PUC authorities or any State Government-recognized body, or must have studied Kannada as a first or second language. Candidates who have not passed a Kannada language test before will be exempted from further Kannada testing only if they score at least 50 out of 150 marks in Kannada in the SSLC-level examination.

Age Limit (as on last date of application)

The minimum age requirement for KSP Armed Police Constable 2026 is 18 years on the last date of application. The maximum age limit varies by category as shown below. The Government of Karnataka provides age relaxation as per GO No. 262 / 2025 (dated 29.01.2026), allowing a one-time relaxation of 5 years in the upper age limit.

Category Maximum Age Limit
General Merit (Male) 33 years
SC / ST / OBC (Category 1, 2A, 2B, 3A, 3B) candidates 35 years
Tribal / Forest community residents of Karnataka (Budakattu) 38 years

Note for Ex-Servicemen: Ex-servicemen are eligible for age relaxation of 3 years in addition to the length of military service rendered. The term "Ex-serviceman" carries the meaning defined in applicable service regulations.

Application Fee - KSP Constable Recruitment 2026

The application fee for KSP Armed Police Constable Recruitment 2026 must be paid online only. Candidates are required to pay the fee before the deadline of 24 July 2026. Fee once paid is non-refundable.

Category Application Fee
General / OBC (Category 2A / 2B / 3A / 3B) ₹750/-
SC / ST (Category A/B/C) / Category-1 / Ex-Servicemen ₹500/-

Fee is non-refundable. Pay online only through the KEA portal.

Selection Process - KSP Armed Police Constable Recruitment 2026

The selection process for KSP Armed Police Constable Recruitment 2026 consists of multiple stages. Candidates must qualify each stage to proceed to the next. The selection is competitive and based on merit at each stage.

  1. Written Examination (Offline - OMR-based)
  2. Physical Standard Test (PST)
  3. Physical Endurance Test (PET)
  4. Medical Examination
  5. Final Merit List and Appointment

Written Examination Pattern

The written exam is of the Offline OMR type and will be held at district-level examination centres across Karnataka. Candidates must download their hall tickets from the official KEA website and carry a valid photo identity proof. The written exam will be conducted at 4 district centres per division. The exam centre cannot be changed under any circumstances.

Paper Subject Total Questions Total Marks Duration
Written Test General Knowledge, Science, Geography, History, Indian Constitution, Current Affairs, Mental Ability, Civic Sense, and Ethical Education 100 100 1½ Hours (90 Minutes)

Written Exam Date: 06 September 2026

  • General Karnataka Division: 10:30 AM to 12:00 PM
  • Kalyana Karnataka Division: 2:30 PM to 4:00 PM

Negative Marking: Yes. Each wrong answer carries a deduction of 0.25 marks. There are 4 options per question and only one correct answer is to be marked. In the OMR sheet, if 5th or subsequent options are marked after originally selecting an answer, candidates must cancel the first answer and wait 5 minutes before marking the new answer; 0.25 marks will be deducted for each wrong answer if the process is not followed correctly.

Note for Ex-Servicemen: As per Government Letter No. BOI 207 / 2018 (dated 05.02.2019), qualified ex-servicemen are selected on merit basis with zero and minimum score benchmarks applicable under those norms.

Also Read: BEML Operator Recruitment 2026 Notification Out

Physical Standard Test (PST)

Candidates who qualify the written examination (shortlisted at a 1:5 ratio per category per vacancy) will be called for the Physical Standard Test. The PST is qualifying in nature and no marks are awarded for it. The PST checks candidates' height and chest measurements.

Candidate Type Minimum Height Minimum Chest
General Male / Ex-Servicemen 168 cm 86 cm (fully expanded) - minimum expansion 5 cm
Budakattu (Forest Tribal) Male Candidates from Karnataka 155 cm Minimum 5 cm expansion; when fully expanded must not be less than 75 cm

Note: Ex-servicemen who do not meet the minimum height of 168 cm will be proportionally considered alongside other qualifying ex-servicemen at the same height. Candidates with lower marks who meet the ex-serviceman minimum height will be considered after all qualifying ex-servicemen are ranked first.

The "Budakattu" (Forest Tribal) community includes candidates from: Uttara Kannada, Dakshina Kannada, Udupi, Chikkamagaluru, Shivamogga, Kodagu, Chamarajanagar, Mysuru forest areas (Siddara, Jenukuruba, Kadukuruba, Yerva, Soliga, Kudiya, Gowdlu, Hasalaru, Malekudiya) and Koraga Budakattu community.

Physical Endurance Test (PET)

The Physical Endurance Test checks a candidate's physical fitness across multiple events. All PST-qualified candidates must complete all PET events in the sequence prescribed. Failing or withdrawing from any event will render the candidate ineligible. PET marks are qualifying only and are not added to the final merit score.

Candidate Type Event Qualifying Standard
General Male Candidates 1600 m Run Within 6 minutes 30 seconds
Long Jump / High Jump Long Jump: Min 3.80 m OR High Jump: Min 1.20 m (3 chances each)
Shot Put (7.26 kg) Minimum 5.60 m (3 chances)
   
Ex-Servicemen 400 m Run Within 2 minutes
Long Jump / High Jump Long Jump: Min 2.50 m OR High Jump: Min 0.90 m (3 chances each)
Shot Put (4 kg) Minimum 3.75 m (3 chances)

Special Note: Candidates appearing for the PET must be physically fit. Any injury during the PET is the sole responsibility of the candidate. Neither the police department nor the recruitment committee is liable for any injury sustained. Candidates must self-certify fitness before participating. All PET events will be videographed for record purposes.

Shortlisting after PST/PET: From candidates who qualify both PST and PET, a shortlist of 1:2 ratio per category per vacancy will be prepared. These shortlisted candidates will be called for the medical examination and final selection. The final selection methodology has been approved by the Government of Karnataka vide GO dated 13.04.2026.

Medical Examination

Candidates shortlisted after PST and PET will appear for a comprehensive medical examination conducted by an authorized Medical Board. The medical exam schedule, venue, and time will be published on the official recruitment portal. Candidates must bring original documents to the medical exam. Admission to the medical exam is based on a provisional list and appearing in the medical exam does not guarantee appointment.

The medical examination covers the following:

a) Vision:

  • Distance Vision: Best eye - 6/9 or 6/9; Worst eye - 6/9 or 6/12
  • Near Vision: 0/6 (Best), 0/8 (Worst)
  • Each eye must have complete field of vision
  • Colour blindness, squint, or any abnormal condition of the eyelid or retina is disqualifying

b) Hearing: Rinne's Test, Weber's Test, and Tests for Vertigo. Any deficiency detected in the above tests is disqualifying.

c) Other Disqualifications:

  • Varicose Veins
  • Impediment in speech
  • Chest X-Ray (and any other tests recommended by the Medical Board)
  • Musculoskeletal Deformities: Knock Knees, Flat Foot, Bow Legs, Cubitus Valgus, Cubitus Varus
  • Any physical or mental disability that prevents the candidate from performing duties

Note: Only physically fit candidates are eligible for appointment. Candidates appearing for PET, written exam, and medical examination are not eligible for any employment benefits. Police personnel who serve and are found medically unfit must not carry any physical disability while on duty.

Training Period and Probation

Selected candidates will undergo basic training at the designated Police Training Schools as prescribed by the DGP and IGP. Candidates who fail in training exams will be discharged from service. After training, selected candidates will serve a probationary period of two years and six months in the Karnataka Police Department.

How to Apply - KSP Armed Police Constable 2026

The application process for KSP Armed Police Constable Recruitment 2026 is entirely online. There is no offline application mode. Candidates must follow the steps below carefully to submit a valid application. Once submitted, no details in the application can be modified or corrected under any circumstances.

  1. Visit the official KEA website: https://cetonline.karnataka.gov.in/kea/
  2. Click on the active recruitment link for "KSP Armed Police Constable 2026"
  3. Register using a valid mobile number and email ID
  4. Fill in all personal, educational, and category details accurately
  5. Upload a recent passport-size photograph in JPEG format (50 KB - 200 KB) and your signature in JPEG format (50 KB - 70 KB)
  6. Pay the application fee online (₹750 or ₹500 depending on category)
  7. Download and save a copy of the submitted application. Keep the fee payment receipt/challan safe until the selection process is complete
  8. Only one application per candidate per division is allowed

Important: Candidates must read all notifications displayed on the official website before applying. Any incorrect information submitted in the application can result in disqualification or criminal action. The mobile number and email ID provided in the application will be used for all future communications. Changes will not be entertained after submission.

The authority conducting correspondence with candidates: Follow the official 'X' account @KEA_KARNATAKA on the web portal for all recruitment-related updates.

KSP Armed Police Constable Recruitment 2026  - Apply Online

The online application window for KSP Armed Police Constable Recruitment 2026 is open from 22 June 2026 to 22 July 2026. The last date to pay the application fee is 24 July 2026. Click the link below to apply directly through the official KEA recruitment portal.

  • Apply Online (KEA Portal): https://cetonline.karnataka.gov.in/kea/
  • KSP Official Website: https://ksp.karnataka.gov.in/

Documents Required at the Time of Application and Later Stages

Candidates must keep the following documents ready when applying online and must produce originals at the time of document verification, PST/PET, and the medical examination. Do NOT carry Aadhaar Card to the examination.

  • Aadhaar Card (for identity verification at application stage only)
  • Marks sheets/certificates for all subjects from the last qualifying examination
  • Date of Birth proof (SSLC/PUC certificate or equivalent)
  • Discharge certificate (for ex-servicemen) and pension / gratuity payment proof
  • Caste/Community certificate in the prescribed format (for SC/ST/OBC candidates)
  • Rural reservation certificate in Form 1 and Form 2 (for rural candidates)
  • Kannada Medium certificate in the prescribed format
  • No-Objection Certificate from the employer (for currently employed candidates)
  • Project Displaced Person (PDP) certificate (if applicable)
  • Permanent Disability certificate (for dependants of deceased / permanently disabled ex-servicemen, if applicable)

Category / Caste Certificate Format

Candidates claiming reservation must submit caste/community certificates in the prescribed format. The format required varies by category:

  • Scheduled Caste / Scheduled Tribe: Form D
  • Category-1 candidates: Form I
  • Category 2A, 2B, 3A, 3B candidates: Form F

The certificate must be current and issued by the concerned Tahsildar. Certificates must be in the prescribed format with the Tahsildar's signature, seal, and barcode / QR code. SC/ST and Category-1 certificates must be valid; OBC certificates (Cat 2A, 2B, 3A, 3B) must not be older than 5 years from the date of application submission. For employment purposes, only caste and income certificates should be submitted (not education or other benefit certificates).

Reservation and Special Category Details

KSP Armed Police Constable Recruitment 2026 provides reservations for various categories as per Karnataka State Government rules. Candidates must apply under the correct category to avail reservation benefits.

Ex-Servicemen (XMP)

As per GO No. DPAR 13 SRR 92 (dated 01.04.1992) and GO No. DPAR 28 SRR 95 (dated 21.10.1995), 10% of posts are reserved for ex-servicemen in direct recruitment. The definition of "ex-serviceman" under Karnataka Civil Services Rules 1977 applies. Dependent family members of ex-servicemen who died in service or who are permanently disabled are also eligible for this reservation.

Persons who quit service voluntarily, those dismissed for misconduct, those who received gratuity and left before completing service, gallantry award winners who are still serving, and persons receiving post-retirement employment pension are NOT eligible under this category.

Rural Candidates

As per GO No. 59 / 2000 (dated 06.01.2001), candidates applying under rural reservation must have studied from Class 1 to Class 10 in a rural area school. The certificate must be submitted in Form 2 with signatures of the school headmaster and field-level education authority. The certificate must be current and issued by the relevant Tahsildar.

Kannada Medium Students (KMS)

As per GO No. 71 (dated 24.10.2002), candidates who have studied in Kannada medium from Class 1 to Class 10 are eligible for KMS reservation. The certificate must be issued by the school headmaster along with a field education officer endorsement, submitted on the last date of application.

Project Displaced Persons (PDP)

As per GO No. 23 / 99 (dated 23.11.2000) and Amendment GO No. 252 / 2020 (Part-1, dated 07.07.2021), displaced family candidates are eligible for reservation as per applicable rules. The certificate must be submitted in the prescribed format by the concerned Tahsildar.

Section 371(J) - Kalyana Karnataka Reservation

For the Kalyana Karnataka division (179 posts), local reservation under Article 371(J) of the Indian Constitution applies as per the Karnataka Public Service (Hyderabad-Karnataka Region Recruitment) Rules, 2013. Candidates claiming this reservation must submit the eligibility certificate in Annexure-2 issued by the competent sub-divisional authority. Original documents must be presented for verification at the time of the medical examination.

Competition Level Analysis - Who Should Apply?

The KSP Armed Police Constable Recruitment 2026 is one of the most competitive state police constable recruitments in Karnataka. With 1600 vacancies and lakhs of eligible PUC-pass candidates across Karnataka, the expected competition level is very high. Here is a realistic overview:

  • Ideal candidates: Physically fit male candidates aged 18-28 years with PUC (Science/Arts/Commerce), strong general knowledge, and regular physical training background have the best chance.
  • Key elimination stages: The written exam (OMR-based) and the PET (1600 m run within 6:30 minutes for general candidates) are the two stages where the largest number of candidates are eliminated.
  • Recommended preparation: Focus on Karnataka-specific general knowledge, current affairs, Indian Constitution, Geography, and Mental Ability for the written exam. Begin physical training immediately - running, long jump, high jump, and shot put practice are essential.
  • Ex-servicemen advantage: Ex-servicemen with the required physical standards have a significant advantage due to easier PET standards and reserved posts.
  • Rural / KMS candidates: Rural reservation and Kannada Medium reservation offer additional advantage. Ensure certificates are in the correct format.

Common Mistakes to Avoid - KSP Constable Application 2026

Many candidates make avoidable errors that lead to rejection of their application. Here are the most common mistakes to avoid when applying for KSP Armed Police Constable Recruitment 2026:

  • Uploading a photograph that is not a recent passport-size JPEG (must be 50 KB - 200 KB)
  • Uploading a signature that exceeds 70 KB or is not in JPEG format
  • Submitting the application without paying the fee - an unpaid application is automatically invalid
  • Applying in the wrong category and submitting incorrect or mismatched caste certificates
  • Applying as a current student (still awaiting PUC results) - this is NOT allowed
  • Submitting multiple applications for the same division - only one application per division is permitted
  • Providing incorrect mobile number or email - all communications including hall ticket links are sent to these details
  • Carrying Aadhaar card alone to the exam centre - at least one photo ID from the approved list is required
  • Ignoring the Kannada language test requirement - candidates who have not previously cleared a Kannada test must be aware of the SSLC-level 50-mark requirement

Eligibility Criteria - Qualification and Age Limit

Candidates checking their eligibility for BEML Operator Recruitment 2026 should know that both educational qualification and age are fixed as on 10 July 2026. This section explains the mandatory ITI qualification and the trade-independent age limit applicable across all five posts.

Educational Qualification (Applicable to All Trades)

  • First-class (60%) marks in the respective ITI trade, along with a National Trade Certificate (NTC) issued by the National Council for Vocational Training (NCVT)
  • Completion of Apprenticeship with a National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC) in the respective trade issued by the Directorate General of Training (DGT)
  • Candidates must have completed the ITI course under the Conventional Training Pattern of the Craftsmen Training Scheme as a regular candidate

Candidates from SC/ST/PwD categories get a 5% relaxation in the minimum qualifying percentage, meaning they need only 55% instead of 60% in their respective trade.

BEML Operator Selection Process 2026 - Step-by-Step

Candidates wondering how BEML will select Operators for these 362 posts can note that the process involves a Computer Based Written Test, document verification, and a pre-employment medical examination, conducted broadly in the sequence below.

  1. Computer Based Written Test: Conducted over 2 hours, with three parts — Part-I: 20 questions on General Awareness, Part-II: 20 questions on English & Reasoning, Part-III: 60 questions on the concerned Discipline. Each question carries 1 mark, and there is no negative marking.
  2. Result and Shortlisting: The qualifying mark is fixed at 45%, relaxed to 40% (5% relaxation) for SC/ST/PwD candidates. Shortlisting is done purely on written test performance.
  3. Document Verification: Candidates are called in order of merit, limited to the number of positions notified per trade/category, where original certificates and one set of self-attested photocopies must be produced.
  4. Travelling Allowance: Candidates who qualify document verification are reimbursed Sleeper Class/II Class train or bus fare by the shortest route, on production of proof of travel.
  5. Provisional Offer and Medical Examination: Candidates clearing document verification receive a Provisional Offer and must undergo a pre-employment medical examination, with no relaxation in health standards.
  6. Final Offer of Engagement: Issued only after a satisfactory medical report is received from the Company's doctor.

Candidates should note that mere fulfilment of eligibility conditions does not guarantee selection, and BEML Management reserves the right to restrict the number of candidates or increase the qualifying percentage based on the volume of applications received.

Troubleshooting and Common Mistakes to Avoid

Many candidates lose out on otherwise eligible applications due to small, avoidable errors. This section highlights frequent mistakes applicants should watch out for while applying for this BEML recruitment.

  • Uploading provisional instead of required documents: NTC provisional certificates are accepted, but candidates should still keep the final certificate ready for the joining stage.
  • Entering an inactive e-mail or mobile number: Since all communication, including offer letters, is sent only via the registered e-mail, candidates should use an ID and number valid for at least one year.
  • Ignoring the OBC-NCL certificate validity: The OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) certificate must not be older than six months as on the last date of online application submission, so candidates should get an updated certificate if their existing one is outdated.

Sports Achievements Considered Up To 31-03-2026

Only sports achievements earned up to 31-03-2026 will count toward the merit list; any achievement after this date will not be considered.

Post-Wise Vacancy, Pay Level & Classification

Each of the three posts under this recruitment carries a different pay level and service classification under the 7th CPC. This section helps candidates understand exactly what each post offers.

Post Vacancies Classification Pay (7th CPC)
Tax Assistant 7 General Central Service, Group 'C', Non-Gazetted, Ministerial Pay Level-4 (Rs. 25,500 – Rs. 81,100)
Stenographer Grade-II 1 General Central Service, Group 'C', Non-Gazetted, Ministerial Pay Level-4 (Rs. 25,500 – Rs. 81,100)
Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS) 4 General Central Service, Group 'C', Non-Gazetted, Non-Ministerial Pay Level-1 (Rs. 18,000 – Rs. 56,900)

Age Limit and Age Relaxation (As on 01-08-2026)

The age limit varies by post, and sportspersons get an additional relaxation on top of the standard limit. This section explains both the base age limit and the relaxation rules.

  • Tax Assistant: 18 to 27 years
  • Stenographer Grade-II: 18 to 27 years
  • Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS): 18 to 25 years

As per DoPT O.M. No. 15012/3/84-Estt.(D) dated 12-11-1987, sportspersons may be allowed a relaxation in the upper age limit of up to a maximum of 5 years (10 years for SC/ST candidates). This relaxation applies only if the candidate fulfils all other eligibility conditions and furnishes a certificate in the prescribed format as per DoPT O.M. No. 1720781414772 dated 04-03-2024.

Educational Qualification & Skill Test Norms

Apart from sports achievement, each post requires a minimum educational qualification, and two of the three posts also have a mandatory typing or stenography skill requirement. Here is the post-wise breakdown.

Tax Assistant

  • Candidates need a Bachelor's Degree from a recognized University or equivalent, along with a data entry speed of 8,000 key depressions per hour.

Stenographer Grade-II

  • Candidates need a 12th class pass or equivalent from a recognized Board/University, and must clear the skill test: dictation of 10 minutes @ 80 words per minute, followed by transcription within 50 minutes in English or 65 minutes in Hindi (on computer).

Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS)

  • Candidates need Matriculation (10th pass) or equivalent from a recognized board. No additional skill test is prescribed for this post.

Who Can Apply: Sports Eligibility Criteria

This recruitment is reserved for candidates with a genuine, verifiable record of representing a state, country, university, or school in recognized sports competitions. Candidates without such achievements are not eligible, regardless of educational qualification.

Applicants must have represented a State or the country in a National or International competition; OR been a medal winner in Junior National Championships, Khelo India Youth Games (above 18 years), Khelo India Winter Games, Khelo India Para Games, Khelo India University Games, or School Games Federation of India (SGFI) events; OR represented their University in Inter-University Tournaments; OR represented a State School Team in National School Games - in any of the eligible sports listed below.

List of Eligible Sports Disciplines

Only achievements in the following sports/games are considered for this recruitment. Candidates should check that their sport is on this list before applying.

Archery, Athletics, Atya-Patya, Badminton, Ball-Badminton, Baseball, Basketball, Billiards & Snookers, Body-Building, Boxing, Bridge, Carrom, Chess, Cricket, Cycling, Cycle Polo, Deaf Sports, Equestrian, Fencing, Football, Golf, Gymnastics, Handball, Hockey, Ice-Hockey, Ice-Skating, Ice-Skiing, Judo, Kabaddi, Karate, Kayaking & Canoeing, Kho-Kho, Kudo, Mallakhamb, Motor Sports, Net Ball, Para Sports (Para Olympics/Para Asian Games disciplines), Pencak Silat, Polo, Powerlifting, Shooting, Shooting Ball, Roll Ball, Roller Skating, Rowing, Rugby, Sepak Takraw, Soft Ball, Soft Tennis, Squash, Swimming, Table Tennis, Taekwondo, Tenni-Koit, Tennis, Tenpin Bowling, Triathlon, Tug-of-war, Volleyball, Weightlifting, Wushu, Wrestling, Yachting, Tennis Ball Cricket, and Yogasana.

Order of Preference for Selection

When multiple eligible candidates apply, the department follows a fixed order of preference laid down by the DoPT, based on the level of competition represented. This section explains exactly how that preference order works.

  1. First preference: Candidates who represented the country in an International Competition with clearance from the Department of Sports.
  2. Second preference: Candidates who represented a State/UT in Senior or Junior National Championships (recognized National Sports Federations) or National Games, winning a medal or position up to 3rd place.
  3. Third preference: Candidates who represented a University in Inter-University competitions or Khelo India University Games, winning a medal or position up to 3rd place.
  4. Fourth preference: Candidates who represented a State/UT in Khelo India Youth Games (above 18 years), Khelo India Winter Games, or Khelo India Para Games, winning a medal or position up to 3rd place.
  5. Fifth preference: Candidates who represented State Schools in National School Games (SGFI) and won a medal or position up to 3rd place.
  6. Sixth preference: Candidates who represented at the levels in categories 2–5 above but did not win a medal or position.

In the event of a tie, candidates with a higher position or more medals are given preference, and individual and team events receive equal preference.

Sports Achievement Scoring Table for Merit List

The final merit list is prepared using a points system based on the level of competition and the position achieved. This table shows exactly how many points each achievement level carries.

A candidate who cannot submit at least one certificate from the authorities listed above need not apply for this recruitment.

Documents Required With the Application

Along with the duly filled application form, candidates must enclose self-attested copies of several supporting documents. Missing any of these can lead to summary rejection.

  • Matriculation/SSC or equivalent certificate (proof of age)
  • Educational qualification certificates, as applicable to the post
  • Caste certificate, for proof of caste (if applicable)
  • Sports/Games certificate (Form 1/2/3/4/5, as applicable)
  • PwBD certificate and UDID card, if applicable
  • No Objection Certificate (NOC) from present employer, if applicable
  • Copy of Aadhaar Card
  • Two recent passport-size photographs

In-Hand Salary Calculator 2026

How to Apply (Offline by Post)

There is no online application option for this recruitment - candidates must apply entirely offline by post. Here is the exact process to follow.

  1. Download and fill the application form as per Annexure-II of the official notification, in block letters using blue/black ball point pen.
  2. Mark your post preference clearly using '1', '2', '3' in order of preference, and 'X' for posts you are not applying for.
  3. Attach self-attested copies of all required documents listed above.
  4. Place the completed application in a closed envelope, superscribed: "Application for appointment of meritorious sportsperson in Income Tax Department, Odisha Region- 2026."
  5. Send the envelope by Registered Post or Speed Post only to: Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax (Hqrs.) (Admn. & Vig.), O/o the Pr. Chief Commissioner of Income Tax, 1st Floor, Aayakar Bhawan, Rajaswa Vihar, Bhubaneswar-751007.
  6. Ensure the application reaches the office by 31-07-2026, 6:00 PM (10-08-2026 for candidates from North Eastern States, Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, and Jammu & Kashmir).

Only one application per candidate is allowed - submitting more than one will result in all applications being rejected. Applications received after the last date will not be considered.

Selection Process

The selection process differs depending on the post applied for. Tax Assistant and Stenographer Grade-II go through two phases, while MTS selection is based on a single merit list.

Tax Assistant & Stenographer Grade-II (Two Phases)

  • In Phase 1, eligible candidates are shortlisted based on their application details and sports achievements. For Tax Assistant, candidates equal to 4 times the number of vacancies (28 candidates) are shortlisted for Phase 2.
  • For Stenographer Grade-II, 10 candidates are shortlisted for Phase 2. In Phase 2, shortlisted candidates appear for a post-specific skill test at the Pr. CCIT Office, Bhubaneswar, at their own expense. The final merit list combines performance from both phases.

Multi-Tasking Staff (Single Phase)

  • Selection for MTS is based purely on the merit list prepared from sports achievement scores, with no separate skill test stage.

Waiting List

  • A waiting list will be maintained: 10 candidates for Tax Assistant, 5 candidates for Stenographer Grade-II, and 10 candidates for MTS.

Pay, Probation & Service Commitment

Beyond the starting pay scale, selected candidates also take on a sport-related service obligation as part of this recruitment. This section explains what is expected after joining.

Selected candidates will be entitled to pay and allowances as per the 7th CPC along with other benefits admissible to Central Government employees, and will be posted in the Odisha Region of the Income Tax Department. They will remain on probation for 2 years, and their participation in departmental tournaments will be a factor in successful completion of probation. Selected candidates are required to represent the Income Tax Department, Odisha in tournaments/meets for at least 5 years.

Doping and Conduct Declaration

This recruitment includes a mandatory anti-doping and conduct clearance requirement that is not common in most government job notifications. Candidates should be aware of this before applying.

Candidates must be clear in all doping tests conducted by WADA, NADA, or any other relevant authority, and must not have been disqualified or banned by any sports federation due to disciplinary action. Any ongoing doping-related investigation must be disclosed. Candidates must also submit a signed self-declaration (as per Annexure-II) covering pending criminal cases, disciplinary action, disqualification, or bans.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Given the strict documentation and postal submission requirements of this recruitment, small errors can lead to outright rejection. The following tips can help candidates avoid common pitfalls.

  • Do not submit more than one application - multiple applications from the same candidate will all be rejected.
  • Do not forget to mark post preference using '1', '2', '3', or 'X' correctly; an unmarked post preference can make the application liable for rejection.
  • Do not send the application without at least one valid sports certificate (Form 1–5) - applications without this will not be considered.
  • Do not send the application through ordinary post or courier - only Registered/Speed Post is accepted.
  • Do not wait until the last day; the application must physically reach the office by 31-07-2026, 6:00 PM, not just be dispatched by that date.
  • Do not claim sports achievements after 31-03-2026 - only achievements up to this date are considered.

Ex-Servicemen who have already secured regular civil employment under the Central Government or Government of NCT of Delhi after availing ESM reservation benefits are not eligible for fee exemption.

Payment must be made only through SBI ePay. No other payment mode will be accepted, and fees paid will not be refunded under any circumstances.

DSSSB Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

Selection will be made through a Computer Based Written Examination under one of three examination schemes depending on the post applied for.

One Tier General (I-T-G) — Post Codes 34/26, 39/26, 40/26: Duration: 2 hours | 200 MCQs | 200 marks. Five sections of 40 marks each: General Awareness, General Intelligence & Reasoning Ability, Arithmetical & Numerical Ability, Hindi Language & Comprehension, and English Language & Comprehension. Final merit is based on written examination marks only.

One Tier Technical (I-T-T) — Post Codes 21/26 to 31/26, 32/26, 33/26, 35/26 to 38/26, 45/26: Duration: 2 hours | 200 MCQs | 200 marks. Section A: 100 marks covering General Awareness, Reasoning, Arithmetic, Hindi, and English (20 marks each). Section B: 100 marks on the domain subject for the post concerned. Minimum qualifying marks apply only to Section B; combined marks of both sections determine the final merit list.

One Tier Technical/Teaching (I-T-T) — Post Codes 41/26, 42/26, 43/26, 44/26: Duration: 2 hours | 200 MCQs | 200 marks. Section A: 100 marks (same five general subjects, 20 marks each). Section B: 100 marks from subject-specific content including teaching methodology/B.Ed. Minimum qualifying marks apply only to Section B; combined marks of both sections determine final merit.

Minimum Qualifying Marks:

Category Minimum Marks
General / EWS 40%
OBC (Delhi) 35%
SC / ST / PwBD 30%
Ex-Servicemen 5% relaxation in respective category (minimum 30%)

Negative marking applies: 0.25 marks will be deducted for each wrong MCQ answer. Skill Test, Aptitude Test, Trade Test, or Physical Endurance Test may be conducted additionally as per job requirements. Marks will be normalized (if required) using the Score Normalisation Based on Deviation Method formula published by DSSSB vide Notice No. 10(271)/Sec.Cell/DSSSB/18/989 dated 11.07.2018.

How to Apply

The application process for DSSSB Recruitment 2026 is entirely online. No applications sent by post, by hand, or by email will be accepted.

  1. Visit the official DSSSB registration and application portal at https://dsssbonline.nic.in.
  2. If you are a new user, complete the one-time registration process. Note down your User ID and password — the same credentials are to be used for all future DSSSB examinations; do not register multiple times.
  3. Log in using your registered credentials and select the relevant post code from Advertisement No. 03/2026.
  4. Fill in all fields of the online application form accurately. Once submitted, no change or correction — including change of category — will be permitted under any circumstances.
  5. Upload a recent, clear colour photograph (plain white or off-white background, full face, front view, eyes open) and your signature. Blurred or illegible photographs/signatures will result in rejection.
  6. Pay the application fee of ₹100 through SBI ePay (exempted categories need not pay).
  7. Submit the form and take a printout for your own records. Keep the registration number and application number safely.

The application portal will be live from 16 June 2026 (12:00 Noon) until 15 July 2026 (11:59 PM), after which the link will be disabled.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Candidates applying for DSSSB 2026 should be careful about a few common pitfalls in the online application process.

Photo and signature uploads are a frequent reason for rejection — ensure the image files are clear, correctly sized, and within the file-size limit specified on the portal. Blurred or illegible uploads will cause outright rejection of candidature. If the payment gateway shows an error after fee deduction, do not immediately retry; wait for a few hours to check whether the payment was credited before attempting again through the portal's payment history section. Use an updated browser (Chrome or Firefox preferred) and avoid mobile browsers for form submission, as they may not render all fields correctly. Save your User ID and password immediately after registration and store your application number carefully — all future communications from DSSSB will reference these. Avoid applying on the last day; DSSSB expressly states it will not be responsible for inability to submit due to heavy server load near the closing date.

BRO GREF Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

All candidates will undergo the recruitment process in the following sequence: (i) Written Examination, (ii) Physical Efficiency Test (PET) including physical measurements and Trade Test (TT) where applicable, (iii) Primary Medical Examination (PME) and Document Verification (DV), and (iv) Induction/Joining. The PET and TT are qualifying in nature - final merit is based solely on written exam marks, subject to qualifying PET, TT, and clearing PME. Minimum passing marks in written exam: 50% for UR/EWS/OBC; 40% for SC/ST. Trade test requires minimum 40% marks to qualify.

Physical Efficiency Test (PET): Candidate must complete 1.6 km (1 mile) run in 10 minutes. PwBD, ESM, Ex-Agniveers, and departmental re-appointment candidates are exempt from PET.

Competition Level Analysis for BRO GREF Recruitment 2026

The competition level for BRO GREF Recruitment 2026 is expected to be moderate to high. The recruitment is restricted to Male candidates only, which reduces the applicant pool compared to open-gender recruitments. However, 899 vacancies across technical/trade posts will attract a large number of ITI-qualified and Matriculation-level candidates, especially for high-vacancy posts like Store Keeper Technical (300) and Operator Communication (261). The written exam followed by PET and Trade Test provides multiple elimination stages, but candidates with relevant ITI trade certificates and physical fitness will have a clear advantage. Ex-Servicemen and Ex-Agniveers get significant age relaxation and weightage, which makes certain trades more competitive in that segment.

The key differentiator here is the offline application process - many eligible candidates may miss out due to postal delays or incorrect application format, effectively reducing actual competition at the written exam stage. Candidates who submit complete and correct applications well before the deadline and prepare trade-specific written exam syllabi will have a significant edge.

Who should NOT apply for BRO GREF Recruitment 2026?

  • Female candidates - this recruitment is strictly for Indian National Males only.
  • Candidates who do not possess the requisite educational/technical qualification as on the closing date of application; those awaiting final exam results are not eligible.
  • Candidates outside the age band 18-27 years as on 01 Jun 2026 (except those eligible for applicable category-based relaxation).
  • OBC candidates from the Creamy Layer - they are not entitled to OBC reservation or age relaxation and must apply as UR/General category.
  • Candidates who cannot meet the region-wise physical standards (height, chest, weight) as physical fitness is mandatory for induction.
  • Candidates with permanent medical conditions listed as grounds for permanent rejection (colour blindness for Drivers/Operators, cardiac conditions, gross myopia, etc.) who cannot pass the Primary Medical Examination at GREF Centre.
  • Candidates unwilling or unable to be posted anywhere in India, especially in remote, high-altitude, or difficult terrain areas in Northern and Eastern regions.
  • Candidates who cannot arrange and send a physical application form with photograph, thumb impression, signature, fee e-receipt, and attested copies by post to Pune - there is no online application mode.
  • Candidates with tattoos on any body part other than the inner forearm (inside elbow to wrist) or reverse palm - tattoos on other parts lead to disqualification at PME.
  • Ex-servicemen who have already joined Govt civil service using ESM benefits and are claiming ESM status again - such candidates are treated as civilian employees.

Common mistakes / What to check before applying BRO GREF Recruitment 2026?

  • Not printing the application form on A4 size 75 GSM bond paper (one side only) and admit card on both sides of a single paper as mandated - non-standard paper leads to rejection.
  • Applying without attaching the e-receipt copy of the application fee paid via SBI Collect; no other payment mode is accepted and missing receipt causes rejection.
  • Sending the application from a wrong/old address instead of present postal address - applications posted from wrong address are rejected to prevent fraudulent claims of 60-day receipt benefit.
  • Not superscribing the envelope with "APPLICATION FOR (NAME OF TRADE/POST) Under Category (UR/SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwBD/ESM/CPL)" as required - unlabelled envelopes may be misdirected.
  • Mismatch between name in application and name in Matriculation certificate - even a dropped or added part of the name requires a Gazette Notification; otherwise candidature is summarily cancelled.
  • Submitting multiple applications for the same post with different details or photographs - this results in lifetime debarment from all GREF examinations.
  • OBC/EWS certificate dated older than one year from the closing date - OBC and EWS certificates must be fresh (not older than one year as on closing date) and in the prescribed Central Govt format.
  • Candidates applying for more than one post/trade using the same envelope - each post requires a separate application with separate fee in a separate envelope.
  • Not carrying the minimum 12 passport-size photographs (same as pasted on application and admit card) to all subsequent recruitment stages - shortage of photos causes disruption at PET/TT/PME stages.
  • Ignoring the trade-specific syllabus and treating the written exam as a general knowledge test - each post has a distinct subject-wise syllabus and candidates must prepare trade-specific topics.

How to Apply for BRO GREF Recruitment 2026

Candidates shall apply offline only; no online application mode is available. Application form and admit card must be downloaded from the official BRO website (www.bro.gov.in) and filled in English or Hindi only, in capital letters. The application form must be printed on A4 size 75 GSM bond paper (one side only) and admit card printed on both sides of a single paper. Candidates must first pay the application fee online via SBI Collect portal and attach the e-receipt copy. Candidates applying for more than one post must send separate applications with separate fee in separate envelopes. Candidates are strongly advised to send applications well before the closing date and not wait for the last day - GREF Centre will not be responsible for postal delays.

Candidates should read the detailed instructions and guidelines available at https://bfsissc.com before applying.

Documents Required to be Enclosed with Application Form:

  • Recent colour passport-size photograph (not older than 1 month from the date of Advertisement) pasted at the prescribed place on application form and admit card - minimum 12 copies of the same photograph to be carried throughout the recruitment process
  • Left hand thumb impression at the prescribed place on application form and admit card
  • Signature of candidate at the prescribed place
  • Copy of e-receipt of application fee paid via SBI Collect
  • Self-attested photostat copies of certificates for essential educational/technical qualifications (Matriculation onwards), date of birth, caste certificate (as per format in Appendix A/B), OBC NCL declaration (Appendix D), EWS certificate (Appendix C), Disability Certificate (Appendix E for PwBD), experience certificate (if applicable), Driving Licence copy (for OEM post)
  • NCC certificate copies (B or C grade), sports certificate, or relationship certificate for Sons of Serving/Ex-GREF personnel - for claiming weightage marks
  • Proof of residence/domicile (for correct physical standards region)
  • Any certificate in language other than Hindi or English must be enclosed with an attested Hindi/English translation by a Group A Gazetted Officer

Send Application (by Postal Service) to: Commandant, GREF Centre, Dighi Camp, Pune - 411015

Printout / physical application is NOT to be sent anywhere else. No hard copy of admit card for written exam will be sent by post - admit card will be posted to the communication address given by the candidate in the admit card.

Application form available at: https://www.bro.gov.in

For queries: Visit https://www.bro.gov.in - all recruitment updates, results, and call letters will be displayed on the BRO website only.

Important Instructions for BRO GREF Recruitment 2026 Candidates

  • Only Male Indian Nationals can apply; Female candidates are not eligible.
  • Application form and/or admit card without signature, without photograph, or without thumb impression will be summarily rejected - no communication will be done for rejected applications.
  • Candidates must ensure their Aadhaar Card photo is current (not older than 2-3 years from written exam date) and address/phone is updated; outdated Aadhaar may prevent entry to the exam.
  • Son of Serving / Ex-GREF staff should write father's GS No., Rank, and Name on top of the application in red ink with a photocopy of relationship certificate, to claim the 15% weightage benefit.
  • Casual Paid Labours (CPL) of GREF who have worked for 179 days in the last one year and are on the Muster Roll on the date of advertisement publication get 10% additional weightage - attach experience certificate signed by OC unit, countersigned by Commander BRTF and verified by Accounts Officer.
  • SC/ST/OBC/EWS candidates who qualify on their own merit (without relaxed standards) will be accommodated against UR vacancies - they must NOT apply separately against UR vacancies.
  • OBC candidates belonging to Creamy Layer are not entitled to reservation; they should apply under UR category.
  • Candidates serving in other Government Departments must apply through proper channel sufficiently in advance; applications not received by due date through proper channel will be rejected.
  • Mobile phones, smartwatches, and all electronic/communication devices are strictly NOT ALLOWED inside GREF Centre, Pune campus during any recruitment process.
  • A candidate who absents himself during any recruitment activity for which he has been called will have his candidature cancelled automatically - he will not be allowed to appear for further stages.
  • There shall be no provision for re-evaluation/re-checking of scores in examination; no correspondence in this regard shall be entertained.
  • Legal jurisdiction for any dispute arising out of this Advertisement shall fall within the jurisdiction of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi.
  • Impersonation or submission of forged documents leads to debarment from all GREF examinations for life/2 years and legal action. GREF has not appointed any agent or coaching centre for action on its behalf - SELECTION WILL BE DONE PURELY ON MERIT IN A TRANSPARENT MANNER.
  • Vacancies are liable to increase/decrease/cancel at any stage without notice due to unforeseen situations.
  • All revisions/corrigendum will be hosted on the BRO website only - candidates should visit www.bro.gov.in regularly.
