About CRE-5: What Is It and Who Is It For?

CRE-5 is a unified, single-window recruitment platform that allows eligible candidates to apply once and be considered for similar posts across multiple participating institutes. The Examination Section, AIIMS New Delhi acts solely as the examination-conducting body; recruitment rules, service conditions, and final appointment decisions rest entirely with each participating institute independently.

Participating organizations are autonomous bodies or subordinate offices under the Government of India, functioning independently from AIIMS New Delhi. Payment can be made via Debit Card, Credit Card, or Net Banking. The examination fee is non-refundable under any circumstances, even if the application is rejected for ineligibility. However, application fees paid by SC/ST candidates who appear in the examination will be refunded to the source account after declaration of results.

AIIMS CRE-5 Recruitment 2026 - Exam Pattern and Syllabus

The CRE-5 Computer Based Test is a structured, time-bound examination designed to assess both domain knowledge and general aptitude.

CBT Structure

Parameter Detail
Duration 90 minutes
Total Questions 100 MCQs
Total Marks 400 marks (4 marks per question)
Negative Marking –1 mark per wrong answer (1/4th deduction)
General Knowledge & Aptitude / Computer 20 MCQs
Domain-Specific Questions 80 MCQs
Sections 5 sections × 20 questions × 18 minutes each

Each section is sequential and time-locked - once a section closes, candidates cannot return to it. Candidates must attempt all possible questions within the active section's time window.

Medium of Examination

Posts where the essential qualification is 10th/12th will be examined in bilingual (English and Hindi) medium. Posts requiring bachelor's or higher qualifications, or posts involving specific technical domain knowledge, will be examined in English only.

Qualifying Marks

Category Qualifying Percentage
UR / EWS 40%
OBC 35%
SC / ST 30%
PwBD (all categories) 30%
Ex-Servicemen As per their category

Tie-Breaking Rules

In case of equal marks, ties are resolved in this order: (i) higher marks in the domain-specific section; (ii) fewer wrong answers/negative marks; (iii) older date of birth; (iv) alphabetical order of name, then father's name, then mother's name.

Full syllabus details for all 57 groups are in Section IX of the official DRA.

Skill Test

For selected post groups, a Skill Test is conducted as Stage II for candidates who qualify the CBT. The skill test is qualifying in nature. The final merit list is prepared based on CBT performance, but only among those who pass the skill test for the relevant post.

Posts requiring skill tests include groups such as Junior Administrative Assistant (typing test), Stenographer (stenography test), Programmer (computer skill test), Hindi Translator (translation test), Assistant Security Officer (PST), and Fire Technician (PET & PST). See Annexure-V of the DRA for complete scheme details.

If a candidate qualifies the CBT but fails the skill test, they remain eligible only for posts within the same group that do not require a skill test.

AIIMS CRE-5 Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

CRE-5 follows a multi-stage recruitment process. Each stage is mandatory for progression to the next.

Stage 1 - Online Application: Candidates register on www.aiimsexams.ac.in and submit applications by 30 June 2026.

Stage 2 - Application Acceptance: Application status published on 9 July 2026.

Stage 3 - Computer Based Test (CBT): Tentatively 25–27 July 2026 at examination centres across major states/UTs of India.

Stage 4 - Skill Test (where applicable): Conducted after CBT for qualifying candidates in applicable groups. Venue: preferably Delhi/NCR. Date to be notified.

Stage 5 - Choice & Preference: Qualified candidates are invited to exercise institute choices and indicate order of preference. Candidates who fail to exercise choices within the given period will not be considered for any institute.

Stage 6 - Seat Allocation: Allocation is made in order of merit based on choices exercised and eligibility at each participating institute.

Stage 7 - Document Verification: Original certificates verified by the respective AIIMS/Institute on the date notified by them.

Stage 8 - Joining: Selected candidates must report on the date specified in the result/allocation notice. Failure to report will lead to mandatory cancellation of candidature for CRE.

AIIMS CRE-5 Recruitment 2026 - How to Apply for AIIMS CRE-5 2026

Applications can only be submitted through the Online Registration Terminal (OTR) at www.aiimsexams.ac.in. Physical documents must not be sent; no correspondence regarding correction in registration will be entertained.

  1. Visit the official website: www.aiimsexams.ac.in
  2. Register through the OTR (One-Time Registration) portal if you have not already done so.
  3. Log in and select the CRE-5 application link.
  4. Fill in all details carefully - name, date of birth, category, qualification, experience, and NOC details if applicable.
  5. Upload photographs, signature, and left thumb impression in the format specified under "Upload Image Instructions."
  6. Select your examination centre preference (state/UT).
  7. Pay the applicable examination fee via Debit Card, Credit Card, or Net Banking.
  8. Submit the application and download the registration slip for your records.
  9. If you are working in a Government/PSU/Autonomous Body, upload the No Objection Certificate (NOC) from your current employer by 6 July 2026 - failing to do so will prevent you from appearing in the examination.
  10. Check your application status on 9 July 2026 at www.aiimsexams.ac.in.

UPSC Recruitment 2026 - Age Relaxation

The standard age relaxations applicable to these posts are as follows. SC candidates receive 5 additional years, OBC candidates receive 3 additional years, and all PwBD candidates receive 10 additional years over and above their category relaxation. For certain posts with a base upper limit of 50 years, the PwBD maximum is capped at 56 years - this applies to the Regional Director (NCONF), Professor Sugar Engineering (NSI), Principal (A&N), and Consultant Ophthalmologist (UT Ladakh). UPSC may relax qualifications and experience at its discretion in writing for candidates otherwise well qualified.

Grade Point to Percentage Conversion (CME Pune and UT Ladakh posts)

Where a grade point system is in use and no conversion formula has been notified by the institution, the following equivalences apply as stated in the notification:

CGPA Equivalent Percentage
6.25 55%

7.75 70%

For UT Ladakh Lecturer and Engineering posts, ST candidates receive a 5% relaxation at Bachelor's and Master's level, making 55% (or equivalent grade) the minimum eligibility.

Special Condition - UT Ladakh Posts (Posts 60-70)

All posts under the Administration of the Union Territory of Ladakh are exclusively open to Domiciles of UT Ladakh. A valid Domicile Certificate issued by the Tehsildar under the Ladakh Civil Services Decentralization and Recruitment Rules, 2025 (published in the Gazette of India on 03.06.2025) is mandatory. Two eligible categories exist: Category A (holders of or eligible for Ladakh Resident Certificate) and Category B (children of LRC holders or those eligible). Reservation is governed by the Jammu and Kashmir Reservation Act, 2004, as extended to UT Ladakh and amended by the Ladakh Reservation (Amendment) Regulation, 2025 (No. 1 of 2025), and further by the Ladakh Reservation (Amendment) Rules, 2025 notified vide S.O. 77 dated 27.06.2025.

UPSC Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

UPSC is conducting this recruitment by selection. The notification does not describe specific stages such as written examination or interview. The selection method will be as determined by UPSC for each post individually. No exam dates or result timelines are stated in the source.

All pay scales are as per the 7th Central Pay Commission Pay Matrix. The level assigned to each post determines the salary band. Key pay levels across these 70 posts are listed below.

Director Grade-II MSME, and all UT Ladakh posts unless otherwise noted. The probation period is 1 year for most Group A posts. For posts under ORGI, the National Pension System (NPS) is applicable with effect from 01.01.2004, and the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) is applicable with effect from 01.04.2025; candidates eligible for NPS have the option to enrol directly under UPS on joining.

UPSC Recruitment 2026- How to Apply

The following steps reflect the application process described in the notification for UPSC's ORA portal.

  1. Visit the UPSC Online Recruitment Application portal at https://upsconline.nic.in/ora/.
  2. Register as a new user if you do not already have an account, or log in with your existing credentials.
  3. Select Advertisement No. 06/2026 from the list and choose the relevant post.
  4. Fill in all required personal, educational, and experience details accurately.
  5. Upload your photograph, signature, and required supporting documents.
  6. Submit the application and save the system-generated confirmation receipt with your registration number.

Troubleshooting and Common Mistakes

Candidates applying through the UPSC ORA portal can avoid common problems by following these general practices. Photograph and signature files must meet the portal's specified size and dimension requirements; uploading files that are too large or in an unsupported format is among the most frequent causes of incomplete applications. If a payment transaction fails, wait for the system to confirm the failure before attempting to pay again - making duplicate payments can cause complications that require manual resolution. Use an updated, stable browser on a desktop or laptop for the best experience; mobile browsers sometimes fail to render form fields correctly. Save your registration number and password immediately after registering, as the portal requires them for every subsequent login. Do not attempt to submit your application on the final day of the application window, as heavy traffic on the server is common and can cause timeouts or session errors.

National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL) has released vacancy notices for 175 posts across two grades - Deputy Engineer / Deputy Chief Controller (34 posts, Vacancy Nos. 21–25/2026) and Junior Engineer / Controller / Train Manager / Station Manager (175 posts, Vacancy Nos. 26–32/2026) - on absorption basis from Regular/Contractual employees of Indian Railways, Government-owned or operated Railways, Metro Railways, and RRTS. These roles support India's first high-speed rail corridor between Mumbai and Ahmedabad. Eligibility criteria are reckoned as on 31 May 2026. Candidates must check the official NHSRCL website for the application portal link and closing date.

NHSRCL DE & JE Recruitment 2026 - Quick Summary

This recruitment covers two distinct pay grades under IDA scales. The Deputy Engineer / Deputy Chief Controller grade carries the NE-6 IDA pay scale of ₹46,000–1,45,000, while the Junior Engineer / Controller / Train Manager / Station Manager grade carries the NE-4 IDA pay scale of ₹40,000–1,25,000. Both grades are open exclusively to serving employees of Indian Railways/Government Railways/Metro Railways/RRTS - this is not an open-market recruitment.

NHSRCL DE & JE Recruitment 2026 - Eligibility Criteria

Eligibility is assessed differently depending on whether the candidate is employed under IDA or CDA pay scales. All experience and eligibility conditions are reckoned as on 31 May 2026. Experience gained through teaching, faculty, apprenticeship, internship, proprietorship, partnership, or freelancing will not count toward the required years of experience.

Work Experience – Deputy Engineer Grade (Vacancy Nos. 21–25/2026)

For IDA pay scale employees (Metro Railways/RRTS):

  • Minimum 5 years' supervisory work experience in the relevant field (Civil/Track maintenance, Electrical Power Distribution, Railway Signalling, Rolling Stock maintenance, or OCC Operations as applicable); AND
  • Currently working in pay scales with minimum bottom pay of ₹46,000, OR
  • 2 years' experience in pay scales with minimum bottom pay of ₹40,000 and above, OR
  • 5 years' experience in pay scales with minimum bottom pay of ₹37,000 and above.

For CDA pay scale employees (Ministry of Railways / other Govt. Railways):

  • Minimum 5 years' supervisory work experience in the relevant field; AND
  • Working in PB-2 + GP ₹4,200 (Level 6 of 7th CPC); AND
  • Minimum 4 years of Group C service.

For the Deputy Chief Controller (Operations) post specifically, candidates under CDA scales must have 5 years' supervisory experience in maintenance of Rolling Stock and Depot Machinery (not OCC operations) to be eligible. Under IDA scales, the requirement is 5 years' post-qualification supervisory experience in OCC/Station/Train operations with minimum 2 years as Traffic Controller in an OCC equipped with modern OCC systems.

Note on MACP: For CDA-scale employees, higher grade pays granted under MACP by the department will not be considered for eligibility. Only the substantive grade is taken into account for determining the grade of absorption.

Work Experience – Junior Engineer Grade (Vacancy Nos. 26–32/2026)

All posts require a minimum of 3 years of post-qualification experience in the relevant field within Operations & Maintenance departments of Indian Railways, Government-owned or operated Railways, Metro Railways, or RRTS systems.

Age Limit

The maximum age limit is 45 years for all posts in both groups. Age is reckoned as on 31 May 2026.

NHSRCL DE & JE Recruitment 2026 - Application Fee

The application fee structure is identical for both vacancy notice groups. Female candidates and candidates from Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe backgrounds are fully exempt from paying the fee. The fee, once paid, is non-refundable under any circumstances - candidates are advised to confirm their eligibility before making payment.

Salary / Pay Scale

NHSRCL offers IDA (Industrial Dearness Allowance) pay scales. The pay and emoluments include Perks, HRA, Medical Benefits, other allowances, EPF, and Gratuity as per extant rules of the corporation.

Grade Pay Scale (IDA)
Deputy Engineer / Deputy Chief Controller (Vacancy Nos. 21–25/2026) ₹46,000–1,45,000 (NE-6)
Junior Engineer / Controller / Train Manager / Station Manager (Vacancy Nos. 26–32/2026) ₹40,000–1,25,000 (NE-4)

NHSRCL DE & JE Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

For the Deputy Engineer grade (Vacancy Nos. 21–25/2026), selection consists of four stages in this order: Computer Based Test (CBT), Document Verification, Interview, and Medical Examination.

For the Junior Engineer grade (Vacancy Nos. 26–32/2026), selection consists of three stages: Computer Based Test (CBT), Document Verification, and Medical Examination. Note that the Interview stage is not part of the JE-grade selection process.

In both cases, management reserves the right to include or dispense with any stage of the selection methodology. Shortlisted candidates will be informed through their registered email addresses. Out-station candidates called for interview (DE grade) will be paid Travelling Allowance as per company rules.

Medical fitness is a mandatory condition of appointment. Candidates will be examined as per the Indian Railway Medical Manual (IRMM). Additional medical tests such as Audiometry and Perimetry may also be conducted as required for safe operation of High Speed Trains.

Surety Bond and Service Commitment

Candidates selected for absorption must be aware of the following binding commitments before joining NHSRCL.

Surety Bond on Joining: Selected candidates must execute a surety bond of ₹3,00,000/- committing to serve NHSRCL for a minimum period of 4 years (excluding any period on Leave Without Pay or Extra-Ordinary Leave). A prior notice of 90 days is required before resigning from the corporation.

Surety Bond on Training: If training is provided, candidates must execute a separate surety bond for the cost of training plus applicable service tax, committing to serve for a minimum of 6 years after training completion. A three-month prior notice is required before resignation in such cases.

Candidates appointed on absorption basis will be on probation for one year. They may be posted anywhere across NHSRCL offices and the MAHSR Project.

Important Note on Controller and Safety Assignment

Candidates applying for posts that include a Controller or Safety assignment (such as Vacancy Nos. 21–29, 31/2026) must indicate their willingness for such assignments in the online application form. They must also furnish their order of preference between the available designations at the time of application. However, the final allocation of post or assignment rests entirely at NHSRCL's discretion, regardless of the candidate's stated preference.

Document Requirements

Along with the application, candidates must submit a Competency Certificate or Experience Certificate issued by their employer. This certificate must clearly indicate the required work experience with year-wise details of the nature and type of work performed. Incomplete applications or applications submitted without supporting documents will be rejected outright.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Applying for NHSRCL absorption posts is a specialized process. Keep the following in mind to avoid rejection:

  • Do not apply for more than one post within the same vacancy notice group (21–25 or 26–32). Only one application is permitted per group, and both CBT sessions may be held simultaneously.
  • Save your registration credentials immediately after creating your portal account. NHSRCL communicates exclusively through registered email IDs - check your spam folder regularly.
  • Verify eligibility before paying the fee. The ₹400 fee is non-refundable under all circumstances, including ineligibility or withdrawal.
  • If your internet connection drops during payment, do not immediately retry - check your bank statement first to avoid a double payment. Contact your bank if the amount is debited but confirmation is not received.
  • Use an updated browser on a stable connection for the application portal. Avoid submitting on the final day to prevent server congestion issues.
  • Ensure your experience certificate is on your employer's letterhead with year-wise work details - general appointment letters or offer letters alone are not acceptable.

Eligibility Criteria for HSSC CET Group D 2026

Eligibility for this CET cycle is built around two simple pillars - educational qualification and age - but each carries specific conditions that can disqualify an otherwise eligible candidate if overlooked.

Educational Qualification

For all Group-D posts except Sweeper, Chowkidar, and Sweeper-cum-Chowkidar, a candidate must hold:

Age Limit and Relaxation

A candidate must be not less than 18 years and not more than 42 years of age as on the closing date of registration (3 July 2026). Age relaxation is governed by Haryana Government instructions dated 25 March 2022, and the upper age limit can extend up to 52 years for candidates entitled to combined relaxation benefits.

A repeated candidate note worth flagging: anyone who already registered for CET Advt. No. 1/2022 (held on 5–6 November 2022) or CET Advt. No. 1/2025 (held on 26–27 July 2025) must use that same CET Registration Number rather than creating a fresh one.

How to Apply Online for HSSC CET Group D 2026

Applications are not submitted on a separate HSSC form - everything runs through Haryana's One Time Registration (OTR) system, which is also used for other state recruitment exams.

  1. Visit the official registration portal at onetimeregn.haryana.gov.in.
  2. New applicants register and receive a Registration Number; returning CET 2022/2025 candidates log in with their existing number.
  3. Fill in personal, educational, and category details accurately, since no corrections are allowed after final submission except during the 7–9 July 2026 edit window.
  4. Upload all category-specific scanned documents (see the documents section below).
  5. Pay the applicable fee online through net banking, debit card, or credit card.
  6. Submit the form, then download and retain a printed copy along with the uploaded documents for future reference.

Apply Online - once live on 19 June 2026, the link will be available through onetimeregn.haryana.gov.in.

Application Fee for HSSC CET Group D 2026

Fee payment follows the category-wise structure set under the CET Policy notified on 31 December 2024, with separate concessions based on residency proof and gender.

Candidates who had already applied and paid fee for CET Group C Advt. No. 1/2025 need not pay the fee again for this Group D cycle. Only candidates applying fresh are required to pay, based on the Standard Rate of Rs. 1,000 (or as revised by the Government).

Category Haryana Resident (with PPN/Aadhaar) Haryana Resident (without PPN/Aadhaar)
General category male applicants 50% of standard rate Standard rate

Two points worth remembering: the fee, once paid, is non-refundable under any circumstances, and a single fee payment covers one CET attempt valid for both Group C and Group D - improving your score in a later attempt requires paying again.

Documents Required for HSSC CET Group D 2026 Application

Every applicant, regardless of category, must upload a common base set of documents, with additional category-specific papers layered on top.

Common documents (all categories):

  • Scanned copy of the Matriculation certificate
  • Latest colour photograph with white background, clearly showing the candidate's name and the date it was taken
  • Scanned signature
  • A signed undertaking as per Annexure VIII of the notification

Category-specific additions:

Category Additional Documents Needed
DSC / OSC Haryana Bonafide Resident certificate + DSC or OSC caste certificate
BC-A / BC-B (Non-Creamy Layer) Haryana Bonafide Resident certificate + BC-A/BC-B certificate issued on or after 1 April 2026
EWS Haryana Bonafide Resident certificate + EWS certificate issued on or after 1 April 2026
Eligible Sports Person (ESP) Haryana Bonafide Resident certificate + Sports Gradation certificate
Ex-Serviceman Haryana Bonafide Resident certificate + Discharge Certificate/Book
Disabled Ex-Serviceman Document showing entry, release, and disability percentage
Family Member of ESM / Disabled ESM Eligibility Certificate issued/renewed on or after 20 June 2025
Dependent of Freedom Fighter Certificate for children/grandchildren of the Freedom Fighter
PwBD Scanned copy of the disability certificate

Only documents uploaded at the time of filling the form are considered for scrutiny - anything submitted later, in any form, will not be entertained.

HSSC CET Group D 2026 Exam Pattern

The CET for Group D is designed as a single-stage, OMR-based screening test rather than a multi-stage exam, making the marking scheme one of the most important things to understand before attempting it.

Feature Detail
Number of Questions 100 MCQs
Total Marks 100
Duration 1 hour 45 minutes
Question Paper Level Secondary Education (Matriculation level)
Language Bilingual - English and Hindi
Mode Offline, OMR-based
Negative Marking for Wrong Answer None
Penalty for Skipped Question -1 mark, but only if the candidate fails to darken the fifth "not attempting" bubble

This last rule is unusual and trips up many candidates: marking a wrong answer carries no penalty at all, but leaving a question blank without filling in the designated fifth circle results in a one-mark deduction. The exam centre, once allotted on the admit card, will not ordinarily be changed.

Also read: SBI PO 2026 Notification PDF Out - Apply Online for 1,500 Probationary Officer Posts

HSSC CET Group D 2026 Syllabus

The CET syllabus is split into two weighted parts - a larger general-skills component and a smaller Haryana-specific component - and the question paper stays at Matriculation difficulty throughout.

Part A: 75% Weightage

  • General Awareness: India and neighbouring countries, especially History, Indian Polity & Constitution, Art & Culture, Geography; General Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
  • Reasoning: Alphabetical order, series, coding-decoding, direction and distance, order and ranking, blood relations, analogy, classification, clock and calendar, mirror/water image, syllogism, sitting arrangement, statement and assumption/conclusion, counting figures, non-verbal series
  • Quantitative Ability: Number system, simplification, decimals, fractions, LCM/HCF, ratio and proportion, percentage, roots, average, profit and loss, discount, simple and compound interest, mensuration, partnership, mixtures and alligation, time and work, time and distance, basic trigonometry, algebra, and geometry
  • English Language: Grammar, spotting errors, fill in the blanks, synonyms and antonyms, spellings, idioms and phrases, sentence improvement, active/passive voice, direct/indirect narration, and tenses
  • Hindi Language: Varna, swar-vyanjan, sangya, sarvanam, visheshan, kriya, kaal, sandhi, samas, paryayvachi-vilom shabd, muhavare-lokoktiyan, and vakya shodhan

Part B: 25% Weightage - Haryana-Specific General Knowledge

This portion covers History, Current Affairs, Literature, Geography, Environment, and Culture of Haryana, along with the state's economy, civics, polity, art, customs, and society.

Minimum Qualifying Marks and Validity of Earlier CET Scores

A general-category candidate needs to score at least 50% in the CET to be eligible, while reserved-category candidates (both vertical and horizontal) get a 10% concession, bringing their qualifying mark to 40%.

For candidates who already cleared the Group D CET held on 12 January 2024 - a score that remains valid until 11 January 2027 - their marks (originally scored out of a maximum of 95) will be mathematically converted into a percentage so they can be merged into the same combined merit list as candidates appearing under the new 100-mark pattern.

It's also worth noting that selection for Group-D posts has changed structurally: under a Government notification dated 12 February 2026, the earlier selection formula (which included up to 10 marks for socio-economic factors such as orphan or widow status alongside the written exam) has been replaced. Selection is now based entirely on CET marks, with no interview at any stage.

HSSC CET (Group D) Syllabus 2026

Reservation Benefits and Certificate Rules

Reservation benefits under this notification are available only to bonafide residents of Haryana State; reserved-category candidates from other states or Union Territories are treated purely as general-category candidates for this recruitment.

BCA and BCB (Non-Creamy Layer)

Certificates must follow the format in Annexure-II and be issued on or after 1 April 2026. Certificates issued for contesting Panchayati Raj elections, or OBC certificates issued for Central Government jobs, are not accepted.

EWS (Economically Weaker Section)

The family's gross annual income must be below Rs. 8 lakh (revised upward from Rs. 6 lakh per the 14 January 2026 instructions), and the family must not own specified assets such as 5+ acres of agricultural land, a 1,000+ sq. ft. residential flat, or immovable property valued at Rs. 1 crore or more. The certificate must be issued on or after 1 April 2026 and is valid only for the financial year it specifies.

DSC and OSC (Deprived and Other Scheduled Castes)

Under instructions dated 13 November 2024, Haryana's existing 20% Scheduled Caste reservation quota is now split equally between Deprived Scheduled Castes (DSC) and Other Scheduled Castes (OSC). If suitable DSC candidates aren't available, the balance posts can go to OSC candidates, and vice versa.

Ex-Servicemen and Freedom Fighter Dependents

Ex-servicemen benefits follow Government Instructions dated 25 May 2026, while reservation for children or grandchildren of Freedom Fighters (paternal or maternal lineage) follows instructions dated 27 October 2021 and 26 April 2022, applicable only when reserved Backward Class or Ex-servicemen posts remain unfilled.

Provisions for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD)

Candidates registering under the PwBD category must select the correct disability code at the time of registration: VH (Visual Impairment), HH (Hard of Hearing), OH (Orthopedic, including locomotor disability and cerebral palsy), or MD (Multiple Disability, including autism and intellectual disability).

Scribe and compensatory time facilities are available as follows:

  • Candidates with blindness, locomotor disability (both arms affected), or cerebral palsy can use a scribe without needing a physical-limitation certificate.
  • Candidates in other PwBD categories need a certificate from a Chief Medical Officer, Civil Surgeon, or Medical Superintendent confirming the need for a scribe.
  • The scribe's own qualification must be up to Matriculation only, and the scribe cannot be a candidate in the same examination.
  • All eligible PwBD candidates referred above receive 20 minutes of compensatory time per hour, bringing the total exam duration to 140 minutes instead of 105.

Selection Process for HSSC CET Group D 2026

Since Group-D recruitment has no separate written exam beyond the CET, the process works differently from Group-C recruitment. The Commission shortlists candidates purely on CET marks, then publishes a category-wise merit and waiting list. When actual posts are advertised later, eligible candidates apply electronically to express willingness for that specific post using their existing Registration Number - only the candidate's consent is sought before the Commission recommends names to the appointing department; there is no fresh written test at this stage.

In case of a tie in CET marks, the older candidate gets precedence; if birth dates also match, the candidate whose first name comes earlier alphabetically (in English) ranks higher.

Exam Day Rules and Malpractice Penalties

HSSC enforces strict frisking and conduct rules at every CET centre, and violations carry debarment periods ranging from two to five years depending on severity.

Items strictly barred inside the exam hall include textual material, calculators, pens, geometry boxes, pen drives, mobile phones, Bluetooth devices, smartwatches, wallets, belts, caps, jewellery, and food or water containers. Candidates wearing articles of religious or cultural faith are advised to report at least two hours before the last reporting time to allow for proper frisking.

Type of Malpractice Debarment Period
Leaving the venue uninformed, or removing exam material from the hall 2 years
Misbehaving with staff, obstructing the exam, or submitting fabricated documents 3 years
Forged admit card/ID, copying, possessing electronic gadgets, impersonation, or hacking exam systems 5 years

OMR sheets must be marked only with a ballpoint pen (not a pencil), and any erasing, scratching, or use of whitener detected by the scanning machine leads to outright cancellation of the OMR sheet and candidature.

Who Should Apply for HSSC CET Group D 2026?

This recruitment cycle is suited to candidates who meet the matriculation-plus-language qualification and fall within the eligible age bracket, with a clear path for reserved-category candidates as well.

You should apply if you:

  • Have passed Matriculation from a recognized board with Hindi or Sanskrit as a subject
  • Are between 18 and 42 years of age as on 3 July 2026, or qualify for a relaxation category
  • Are a bonafide resident of Haryana seeking reservation benefits, or are applying as a general-category candidate from anywhere in India, Nepal, or Bhutan

You should reconsider applying if you:

  • Do not hold Matriculation, or did not study Hindi/Sanskrit up to that level
  • Fall outside the 18–42 age band without an applicable relaxation
  • Are a reserved-category candidate from outside Haryana expecting reservation benefits - you will only be considered under the general category

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Several avoidable errors lead to rejection at the scrutiny stage or loss of marks during the exam itself, based directly on the causes of rejection listed in the notification.

  • Uploading a BCA, BCB, EWS, or DSC/OSC certificate dated outside its required validity window
  • Submitting an incomplete document set for your claimed category
  • Registering more than once instead of using an existing CET 2022 or 2025 Registration Number
  • Leaving a question blank without filling the fifth "not attempted" bubble, resulting in an avoidable -1 mark
  • Darkening more than one circle for a single question, which voids that answer entirely
  • Assuming corrections can be made after final submission - they are only possible during the 7–9 July 2026 window
  • Carrying barred items such as mobile phones, watches, or wallets into the exam hall

Eligibility Criteria for Medical Assistant and Pharmacist Trade

Eligibility for this recruitment differs based on whether a candidate is applying with a 10+2 qualification or with a Diploma/B.Pharma/B.Sc in Pharmacy. This section explains both eligibility streams along with the applicable age brackets.

Stream 1: Medical Assistant Trade (10+2 Candidates)

  • Candidate should be unmarried
  • Date of birth should fall between 01 July 2006 and 01 July 2010 (both dates inclusive)

Stream 2: Medical Assistant (Pharmacist) Trade - Diploma/B.Pharma/B.Sc in Pharmacy

  • Unmarried candidates: Date of birth between 01 July 2003 and 01 July 2008 (both dates inclusive)
  • Married candidates: Date of birth between 01 July 2003 and 01 July 2006 (both dates inclusive)

Upper Age Limit on Date of Enrolment

Candidate Category Maximum Age on Date of Enrolment

Educational Qualification for IAF Medical Assistant Trade

This section details the minimum academic requirements that determine whether a candidate qualifies for the Medical Assistant trade under either eligibility stream.

For 10+2 Candidates

Candidates should have passed 10+2/Intermediate/Equivalent with Physics, Chemistry, Biology, and English from a Board recognised by Central, State, or UT authorities, securing a minimum of 50% marks in aggregate and 50% marks in English. Alternatively, a two-year vocational course with non-vocational subjects of Physics, Chemistry, Biology, and English with the same percentage criteria is also accepted.

For Diploma / B.Pharma / B.Sc in Pharmacy Candidates

Candidates must have passed Intermediate/10+2/Equivalent with Physics, Chemistry, Biology, and English with a minimum of 50% marks in aggregate and 50% marks in English, in addition to holding a Diploma/B.Pharma/B.Sc in Pharmacy with at least 50% aggregate marks and valid registration with the State Pharmacy Council or Pharmacy Council of India (PCI) at the time of enrolment.

Note: The exact aggregate percentage before decimal, as printed on the marksheet, will be considered — for example, 49.99% will be treated as 49% and not rounded off to 50%.

Stage Amount

Job Profile of a Medical Assistant in the Indian Air Force

This section explains what duties a selected candidate will actually perform after being trained and posted as a Medical Assistant.

As a Medical Assistant, candidates are trained in nursing and first-aid, and are involved in the management of medical stores, dispensaries, ward supervision, and other Air Force duties as assigned by superior authorities.

Tenure and Training Details

This section explains the service commitment and training structure that selected candidates undergo after enrolment.

  • Initial enrolment period: 20 years, extendable up to the age of 57 years (subject to service conditions)
  • Candidates undergo Joint Basic Phase Training (JBPT) followed by trade-specific training, which may include security training
  • Trade allotted will not be changed on a candidate's request under any grounds
  • Candidates are not permitted to stay with family during training, and unmarried candidates cannot marry until ab-initio training is complete

Selection Process - Phase-I, Phase-II and Phase-III

The selection procedure for this Indian Air Force Pharmacist Recruitment 2026 is conducted in three phases. This section explains what each phase involves and how candidates progress through the process.

Phase-I: Online Written Test

  • Duration: 45 minutes
  • Subjects: English (as per 10+2 CBSE syllabus) and Reasoning & General Awareness (RAGA)
  • Marking: +1 for every correct answer, 0 for unattempted questions, -0.25 for each wrong answer
  • Candidates must qualify in each paper separately; marks may be normalised across sessions

Phase-II: Physical Fitness Test, Adaptability Test and Document Verification

Physical Fitness Test (PFT):

Test Maximum Time (up to 21 years) Maximum Time (above 21 / Diploma-Pharma candidates)
1.6 Km Run Within 7 minutes Within 7 minutes 30 seconds

Candidates who clear the run undergo PFT-II after a 10-minute recuperation break, consisting of 10 push-ups, 10 sit-ups, and 20 squats, each within one minute, with short breaks between exercises.

  • Candidates who pass PFT undertake Adaptability Test-I (objective written test)
  • Candidates clearing Adaptability Test-I proceed to Adaptability Test-II as per current policy
  • Document verification of educational and other certificates is also carried out at this stage

Phase-III: Medical Examination

Candidates who qualify Adaptability Test-II are issued a medical appointment letter and undergo a detailed medical examination conducted by the Air Force Medical Team, including blood haemogram, urine routine examination, biochemistry tests (blood sugar, serum cholesterol, RFT, LFT), chest radiograph, and ECG.

Candidates declared medically unfit may apply for an Appeal Medical Board (AMB) by depositing Rs. 40/- within three working days of the medical examination.

This section lists the documents candidates must carry when reporting for Phase-II at the designated Airmen Selection Centre (ASC), as document verification is a mandatory part of the selection process.

  • Colour printout of Phase-II Admit Card and original Phase-I Admit Card
  • Colour printout of the duly filled online application form
  • HB pencil, eraser, sharpener, glue stick, stapler, and black/blue ball point pen
  • Eight unattested passport-size colour photographs (same as used during registration)
  • Original/DigiLocker verified printout and four self-attested photocopies of matriculation certificate
  • Original/DigiLocker verified printout and four self-attested photocopies of 10+2/Diploma/B.Pharma/B.Sc Pharmacy certificates and marksheets
  • NCC 'A', 'B', or 'C' certificate, if applicable
  • NOC from employer for serving government employees, or Discharge Certificate for ex-servicemen, if applicable
  • Original AADHAAR Card (mandatory for Phase-I testing as well)

How to Apply Online for IAF Airmen Medical Assistant Recruitment 2026

This section provides the step-by-step process to successfully register and submit the online application on the official CASB web portal.

  1. Visit the official CASB recruitment portal at https://iafrecruitment.edcil.co.in
  2. Complete Step-I registration by entering personal and contact details, then generate and verify OTPs sent to your e-mail ID and mobile number
  3. Receive your User ID and Password via e-mail/SMS, then click "Go To Application"
  4. Complete Step-II by filling Personal Details, Communication Details, Qualification Details, Declaration, and uploading required documents
  5. Upload scanned photograph (100-200 KB), signature (80-150 KB), left thumb impression (50-100 KB), and parent's signature if below 18 years of age, all in .jpg/.jpeg format
  6. Capture a live image for facial verification against the uploaded photograph
  7. Preview the filled application and correct any errors before final submission
  8. Pay the non-refundable examination fee of Rs. 550/- plus 18% GST through the Payment Gateway
  9. Print and save the submitted application form in PDF for future reference

Candidates can use the Apply Online facility only between 06 July 2026, 1100 Hr and 26 July 2026, 2300 Hr. Each candidate should apply only once; multiple applications will lead to rejection of candidature.

Important General Instructions

This section highlights additional rules candidates must follow while applying and appearing for the selection test.

  • Candidates must indicate five choices of examination city and fourteen choices of ASC for Phase-II in order of preference
  • Requests for change of examination centre or date will not be entertained
  • Mobile phones, smart watches, and electronic devices are strictly prohibited in testing areas during Phase-I and Phase-II

  • No bribe is required at any stage; candidates should beware of unscrupulous agents posing as recruiters
  • Any corrigendum or update will be published only on the CASB web portal, not in newspapers or other media

Nature of Employment: Fixed Term, Not Permanent

Candidates exploring this opportunity should understand that these are not regular permanent bank jobs. Bank of Baroda has clearly defined the engagement structure for these IT positions.

Selected candidates will be engaged as an Officer on Fixed Term Employment for an initial period of 3 years from the date of joining. This can be renewed or extended for an additional maximum of 2 years, subject to satisfactory performance and at the Bank's discretion. The engagement automatically ends on expiry unless renewed, and in any case, it remains valid only till the candidate reaches a maximum age of 60 years or the end of the fixed term, whichever comes first.

Eligibility Criteria

Eligibility for these IT leadership roles is assessed as on the cut-off date, and the Bank has linked position-specific qualification and experience details separately for each post rather than listing them within the main notification.

The detailed educational qualification and work experience criteria for each of the 5 posts - VP Head-AI, VP Head Platform Engineering, DVP Dy. Head Cloud CoE, DVP Dy. Head IT Infrastructure, and DVP Dy. Head Platform Engineering - are provided through separate position-specific links on the Bank's official notification, since each senior IT role has its own distinct skill and experience requirements.

General Eligibility Conditions

  • Eligibility is reckoned as on the cut-off date of 01-06-2026.
  • Post-qualification experience of less than six months in any organization as on 01-06-2026 will not be counted toward eligibility, unless that experience is part of the candidate's current employment.
  • Candidates must be a Citizen of India, or fall under specific categories such as a subject of Nepal or Bhutan, a Tibetan refugee who settled in India before 1 January 1962, or a person of Indian origin who migrated from select countries with the intention of permanently settling in India.
  • OBC candidates falling under the "creamy layer" are not entitled to OBC reservation or age relaxation and must apply under the General category.

VP Head Platform Engineering B.E./ B.Tech. in Computer Science or Information Technology/ Electronics & Tele Communication/ Electrical & Electronics OR MCA
DVP Dy. Head Cloud CoE (Centre of Excellence) B.E./ B.Tech. in Computer Science or Information Technology/ Electronics & Tele Communication/ Electrical & Electronics OR MCA

Application Fee

Candidates often want to know the cost of applying before starting their application. For this recruitment, Bank of Baroda has kept the process completely free.

The application fee is Nil for all categories of candidates applying for these 5 IT positions.

CIBIL Score and Credit History Requirement

Unlike most government job notifications, this Bank of Baroda recruitment includes a specific financial credibility check. This is an important and somewhat unique eligibility condition candidates must be aware of.

Candidates must maintain a satisfactory credit history, and a minimum CIBIL score of 680 or above is required at the time of joining. Candidates who have defaulted on loan repayment or credit card dues, or against whom adverse reports exist from CIBIL or other external credit rating agencies, will be deemed ineligible for appointment. The Bank reserves the right to reject candidature at any stage, including after joining, if the credit profile is found unsatisfactory.

Remuneration and Location of Posting

Salary for these roles is not fixed on a standard pay scale, unlike typical government recruitment. This section explains how pay is determined and where selected candidates will be posted.

Remuneration will be offered based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, overall suitability, last drawn salary, and market benchmark - there is no fixed pay scale mentioned in the notification. The location of posting is Mumbai or Hyderabad, though selected candidates remain liable for transfer anywhere in India as per the Bank's requirement.

Selection Process

Selection for these IT leadership posts goes beyond a standard written exam, with the Bank assessing multiple professional parameters. No fixed exam date or selection timeline has been announced in the notification.

The selection process may include an online test, a psychometric test, or any other test the Bank deems suitable, followed by an Interview or multiple interviews. The Bank may shortlist applications based on criteria such as suitability for the role, depth of prior experience, leadership exposure, domain expertise, professional certifications, and exposure to regulatory or compliance frameworks. The minimum qualifying mark for the Personal Interview (PI) is 60% for UR category and 55% for Reserved category candidates.

How to Apply Online for Bank of Baroda IT Recruitment 2026

Applications for these posts can only be submitted online, with no other mode accepted. Here is the step-by-step process candidates need to follow.

  1. Visit the Bank's official website and go to the Career section → Current Opportunities page.
  2. Register online using the application format enabled for this recruitment.
  3. Fill in the online application form carefully, since no changes are allowed after clicking SUBMIT.
  4. Upload your Bio-data, scanned photograph, signature, and supporting eligibility documents as per the prescribed specifications.
  5. Verify all entered details, including name, category, date of birth, and post applied for, before final submission.
  6. Submit the application well before 10-07-2026 to avoid last-minute website load issues.
  7. Save the acknowledgement number generated on the portal and check your registered email for confirmation - registration is complete only once this acknowledgement is received.

Documents and Upload Specifications

Bank of Baroda requires specific documents to be uploaded at the time of application, each with strict file format and size requirements. Getting these specifications wrong is a common reason applications get stuck.

Documents to Upload (Application Stage)

  • Resume (PDF)
  • DOB Proof: 10th marksheet/certificate (PDF)
  • Educational Certificates: relevant mark-sheets/certificates, scanned in a single PDF file
  • Work experience certificates, if applicable (PDF)
  • Caste/Category Certificate, if applicable (PDF)
  • PWD certificate, if applicable (PDF)

Photograph and Signature Specifications

  • Photograph: recent passport-style colour picture, dimensions 200 x 230 pixels, file size between 20kb–50kb.
  • Signature: signed in black ink on white paper, dimensions 140 x 60 pixels, file size between 10kb–20kb.
  • Document files: must be in PDF format, A4 page size, and not exceeding 500 KB each.

Documents Required at Interview Stage

At the time of interview, candidates must produce originals along with self-attested photocopies of documents including the call letter printout, system-generated application printout, date of birth proof, photo identity proof, mark sheets and degree certificates, and category certificates where applicable. Notably, a Ration Card will not be accepted as valid identity proof for this recruitment.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Given the strict, no-correction-after-submission policy of this recruitment, small errors can have a big impact. The following points can help candidates avoid losing their candidature.

  • Do not submit the application without double-checking every field - no changes are allowed once you click SUBMIT.
  • Do not upload a photograph or signature outside the specified pixel and file-size limits, as the system will reject non-compliant files.
  • Do not assume your credit history is irrelevant - a CIBIL score below 680 or any adverse credit report can make you ineligible.
  • Do not delay applying until the last day; server load near the 10-07-2026 deadline can prevent successful submission.
  • Do not carry a Ration Card as your only ID proof for the interview - it will not be accepted.
  • Do not forget to check the position-specific eligibility link for your chosen post, since detailed qualifications differ by role.

Important Links

All application and update activity for this recruitment happens only through the Bank's official website. Candidates should bookmark this page and avoid relying on any third-party links.

Northeast Frontier Railway (NFR) has released Employment Notice No. 03/2026, inviting applications for 22 posts under the Scouts & Guides Quota for the year 2026-27 - 12 posts in Level-2 (Grade Pay Rs. 1900/-) and 10 posts in Level-1 (Grade Pay Rs. 1800/-). The notification was issued on 20-06-2026, and the closing date is 19-07-2026. Only candidates holding a valid Scouts & Guides qualification are eligible; candidates without this qualification cannot apply.

Add FJA on  As Preferred Source

NFR Recruitment 2026 - Overview

Before going into the detailed eligibility conditions, here are the essential facts about this NFR recruitment that candidates need to know first.

  • Recruiting Body: Northeast Frontier Railway (NFR)
  • Notice Number: Employment Notice No. 03/2026
  • Recruitment Type: Against Scouts & Guides Quota
  • Recruitment Year: 2026-27
  • Total Posts: 22 (Level-2: 12, Level-1: 10)
  • Date of Notification: 20-06-2026

  • Mandatory Requirement: Valid Scout/Guide qualification (candidates without it are not eligible)

NFR has set a standard closing date for most applicants, with an extended window for candidates from specific remote regions. This section explains exactly which date applies to which candidates.

NFR Recruitment 2026: Post-Wise Vacancy and Pay Details

The 22 vacancies are spread across two pay levels under the 7th Pay Commission Pay Matrix. Each level has its own qualification and age requirements, detailed separately below.

Level-2 Posts (Grade Pay Rs. 1900/-) - 12 Vacancies

  • These 12 posts fall under Group 'C' and are placed at Level-2 of the Pay Matrix, carrying a Grade Pay of Rs. 1,900/- as per the 7th Pay Commission.

Level-1 Posts (Grade Pay Rs. 1800/-) - 10 Vacancies

  • These 10 posts fall under the erstwhile Group 'D' category and are placed at Level-1 of the Pay Matrix, carrying a Grade Pay of Rs. 1,800/- as per the 7th Pay Commission.

Age Limit (As on 01-07-2026)

The age limit differs by pay level and category. Candidates should check their applicable age band carefully before applying, since the reference date for age calculation is 01-07-2026.

Category Level-2 (GP 1900) Level-1 (GP 1800)
UR (Unreserved) 18 to 30 years 18 to 33 years
OBC 18 to 33 years 18 to 36 years
SC/ST 18 to 35 years 18 to 38 years

Educational Qualification for Level-2 Posts

For the 12 Level-2 posts, NFR has prescribed a general qualification along with separate conditions for two specific categories of posts - Clerk-cum-Typist and Artisan (Technical).

  • Pass in 12th (+2 stage) or its equivalent examination with not less than 50% marks in aggregate.
  • The 50% aggregate condition is relaxed for ST/SC and Ex-Servicemen candidates, and is not insisted upon where the candidate holds a higher qualification such as Graduation or Post-Graduation.
  • For Jr. Clerk cum Typist / Accounts Clerk cum Typist posts (based on vacancy), typing proficiency of 30 wpm in English or 25 wpm in Hindi is essential.
  • For Artisan (Technical Categories) posts, candidates need a pass in Matriculation or equivalent from a recognized board along with an ITI certificate. A Diploma in Engineering is not considered as an alternative higher qualification for this post.

Educational Qualification for Level-1 Posts

For the 10 Level-1 posts, the educational requirement is centered around ITI training rather than a 12th-pass qualification.

  • 10th pass along with an ITI certificate from an institution recognized by NCVT/SCVT or its equivalent.
  • Alternatively, candidates holding a National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC) granted by NCVT are also eligible.

Mandatory Scouts & Guides Qualification

This recruitment is exclusively for candidates with a genuine, verifiable background in the Scouts & Guides movement. Candidates lacking any of the conditions below are not eligible to apply, regardless of educational qualification.

  • Must hold the rank of President Scout / President Guide / Rover / Ranger, OR be a holder of the Himalayan Wood Badge (HWB) in any section.
  • Must have been an active member of a Scouts organization for the last 5 years, i.e., from 01-04-2019 onwards. This must be proven through a "Certificate of Activeness" as per Annexure-C (original).
  • Must have attended two events at National Level or All India Railways level, AND two events at State level.
  • Explanatory note: Activeness must be shown for at least 5 years in the recent past - covering 2019-20, 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 - and the candidate must continue to remain active till date.

Division-Wise Distribution of Posts

NFR has specified that a fixed number of posts are earmarked per railway division under this recruitment. This helps candidates understand where these vacancies are physically located.

As per the notification, 2 posts are allotted per Railway Division across the following five divisions: Tinsukia, Lumding, Rangiya, Alipurduar, and Katihar.

Can You Apply for Both Level-2 and Level-1 Posts?

NFR has clarified how the selection process and applications work when a candidate is eligible for posts at both levels.

The selection for Group 'C' (Level-2) and erstwhile Group 'D' (Level-1) will be conducted separately. A candidate is allowed to apply for both Level-2 (GP Rs. 1900/-) and Level-1 (GP Rs. 1800/-) posts, but must do so by submitting a separate application for each level.

NFR Recruitment 2026 PDF Download Link & Apply 

Candidates can access the complete official notification and the application process directly from the Northeast Frontier Railway's official website. The detailed notification carries the full eligibility annexures, application format, and submission instructions.

Resource Link
PDF Download Link (Official Notification) Click Here - Employment News
Official Website https://nfr.indianrailways.gov.in/

On the website, navigate through: General Info → Recruitment Notifications (Sports, Scouts & Guides and Cultural) → Recruitment against Scouts & Guides Quota to find the full notification and application link.

How This Recruitment Differs From a Regular RRB Recruitment

Many candidates confuse Scouts & Guides quota recruitment with regular RRB recruitment drives. Here's what sets it apart.

Unlike standard RRB recruitment, which is open to all eligible candidates purely on educational qualification and a competitive written exam, this NFR drive is a quota-based recruitment exclusively for Scouts & Guides achievers. Eligibility depends heavily on verified Scout/Guide activity records (Annexure-C), national/state-level event participation, and continuous activeness - not solely on academic marks or a written test. Candidates without a genuine Scouts & Guides background, however well-qualified academically, cannot apply under this notice.

Common Mistakes Candidates Should Avoid

Since this is a specialized quota recruitment, candidates often make avoidable errors. The points below can help applicants avoid rejection.

  • Do not apply without a valid President Scout/Guide, Rover/Ranger rank, or HWB certification - applications without this are not eligible.
  • Do not skip getting the Certificate of Activeness in the correct Annexure-C format; this is a mandatory original document.
  • Do not assume Diploma in Engineering qualifies as a higher qualification for the Artisan post under Level-2 - it does not, as per the notification.
  • If applying for both Level-2 and Level-1, remember to submit two separate applications, not a single combined one.
  • Candidates from general regions should not wait beyond 19-07-2026; only the specified remote regions get the extended 29-07-2026 deadline.

Eligibility Criteria for Each Post

Eligibility for Pawan Hans Recruitment 2026 varies significantly by post, ranging from a basic graduate degree to specialised aviation diplomas. The breakdown below covers the exact qualification and experience required for each role.

Assistant (HR&A) - Regular and Contractual

For the Regular basis post, candidates need a Graduate Degree in any discipline with 3 years of post-qualification experience in the relevant field, OR an MBA/PG Degree/2-year Diploma in HR/HRM/HRD/PM & IR with 1 year of post-qualification experience. For the Contractual basis post, the requirement is Graduation with 3 years post-qualification experience, OR Graduation with a 2-year Diploma in IR&PM plus 1 year of relevant experience.

Junior Engineer (Civil) - Contract Basis

This post requires a Diploma in Civil Engineering from a recognised institute, with a minimum of 5 years of post-qualification experience in preparing estimates, Bill of Quantity (BoQ), and tenders for repair and maintenance work. Experience in civil maintenance of large buildings, malls, metro stations, and high-rise apartments is required, and knowledge of computers is preferable.

Quality Assistant and Assistant (CAMO) - Contract Basis

Both these aviation-focused roles require a Diploma in AME/Aeronautical or BSc in Aviation, along with 3 years of aviation experience - specifically in Quality CAR-145 for the Quality Assistant post, and in CAMO (Continuing Airworthiness Management Organisation) for the Assistant (CAMO) post.

How to Apply for Pawan Hans Recruitment 2026

Pawan Hans accepts applications through a combined online-plus-postal process, meaning an online submission alone is not sufficient - a signed hard copy must also reach the office by the deadline. Candidates unable to apply online can also use an offline route.

  1. Visit the Careers tab on www.pawanhans.co.in and apply online.
  2. Take a printout of the duly filled and signed online application form.
  3. Affix a recent passport-size photograph on the printed form.
  4. Attach self-attested copies of testimonials supporting age, caste/class, qualification, experience, Pay/CTC, and licence/medical status.
  5. Send the complete application through proper channel to reach the office on or before 10 July 2026.

Documents Required for Application

Candidates preparing their application should keep self-attested copies of the following documents ready, since applications without supporting proof are liable to rejection.

  • Proof of age (e.g., Matriculation certificate)

  • Educational qualification certificates matching the post applied for
  • Experience certificates showing post-qualification experience (teaching experience and training/induction periods are not counted)
  • Proof of Pay/CTC in current or previous employment
  • Licence/medical status documents, particularly for aviation-related posts like Quality Assistant, Assistant (CAMO), and Trainee Technician

All qualifications must be from Universities/Institutions recognised by UGC/AICTE or other appropriate statutory authorities in India.

Selection Process and General Conditions

Pawan Hans follows a merit-based shortlisting process rather than calling every eligible applicant, giving the management discretion over each stage of recruitment.

  • The management will call only candidates ranking highest on eligibility criteria - mere eligibility does not guarantee a test call.
  • The number of candidates called for test may be restricted based on the response received for each post.
  • The management reserves the right to reject applications, cancel posts, or relax age/experience/qualification criteria at its discretion.
  • Only post-qualification experience is counted - teaching experience and induction/training periods are excluded.
  • Candidates called for the test must produce all original documents at the time of test; failure to do so means they will not be permitted to appear, and travelling allowance will not be reimbursed.
  • Outstation candidates called for the test are reimbursed 2nd Class Rail/Bus fare by the shortest route, subject to proof of journey.
  • All appointments are subject to medical fitness as per Pawan Hans Limited rules.
  • Selected candidates may be transferred anywhere in India or abroad at the Management's discretion.
  • Persons with disability of not less than 40% as per GOI guidelines are eligible for PwD benefits.

Common Mistakes Candidates Should Avoid

Many applicants risk rejection due to procedural errors rather than lack of eligibility. Reviewing these common pitfalls before applying can help ensure a smooth submission.

  • Forgetting the postal submission step: Applying online alone is not enough - the signed printout with photograph and testimonials must physically reach the Delhi office by 10 July 2026.
  • Submitting one application for multiple posts: Candidates interested in more than one post must submit a separate application for each, or only the first post mentioned will be considered.
  • Skipping self-attestation: Submitting unattested or incomplete testimonial copies can lead to outright rejection of the application.
  • Ignoring the Demand Draft requirement for offline applications: Offline applicants who haven't paid online must enclose a Rs. 354 DD in favour of Pawan Hans Limited - applications without proof of fee payment are liable to rejection (except for exempted SC/ST/PwD candidates).
  • Counting ineligible experience: Teaching experience and induction/training periods do not count toward the required post-qualification experience - only genuine post-qualification work experience is considered.
  • Missing original documents at the test stage: Candidates who don't bring original documents (qualification, experience, Pay/CTC, reservation proof) to the test will not be permitted to appear and will lose travel allowance reimbursement.
  • Relying on newspaper notices for updates: Pawan Hans publishes all corrigenda, addenda, or cancellations only on its website, not in newspapers, so candidates must check www.pawanhans.co.in regularly.

About SDSC SHAR and the Space Central Schools

This section explains who SDSC SHAR is and why it is hiring teachers, which helps candidates understand the nature of the employer before applying.

Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota (SDSC SHAR) is India's spaceport, functioning under the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), Department of Space, Government of India. It is located 100 km north of Chennai on National Highway 05, in Tirupati District, Andhra Pradesh. SDSC SHAR operates Space Central Schools at its Sriharikota and Sullurpeta campuses under the NCERT/CBSE curriculum, primarily to educate the children of its employees and supporting personnel. To staff these schools, SDSC SHAR has invited online applications for five categories of teaching posts.

Post-Wise Vacancy Details (10 Posts)

Candidates checking how many posts are open and in which subject can refer to the table below, which lists all five post codes notified by SDSC SHAR along with their reserved category and vacancy count.

Post Code Post Name Vacancies & Category
01 Trained Graduate Teacher (Maths) - to teach Maths & Physics UR-01
02 Trained Graduate Teacher (Science) - to teach Chemistry & Biology SC-01
03 Trained Graduate Teacher - Work Experience Teacher (WET) UR-01
04 Trained Graduate Teacher (Telugu) ST-01
05 Primary Teacher UR-03, EWS-01, OBC-02 (1 OBC backlog)

Of the six Primary Teacher vacancies, one post is identified for PwBD (LDCP) backlog vacancy. If a suitable PwBD (LDCP) candidate is not found, the post will be offered to a candidate with any other benchmark disability except blindness, and if still unfilled, it will revert to the vertical reservation category. All posts are currently temporary in nature but are likely to continue.

Also read: ESIC Medical College & Hospital Surat Recruitment 2026

Eligibility Criteria for Each Teaching Post

Each post carries a distinct qualification requirement linked to the subject taught. The table-style breakdown below summarises the core academic and teaching-eligibility requirements for every post code.

TGT (Maths) - To Teach Maths and Physics

Candidates need a four-year NCTE-recognised integrated degree with at least 50% marks (subject + B.Ed component), OR a Bachelor's/Honours degree with 50% marks plus a B.Ed degree from an NCTE-recognised institution (alternatives include a 3-year integrated B.Ed-M.Ed or a 1-year B.Ed Special Education from RCI). Candidates must also have qualified CTET Paper-II and be able to teach in Hindi and English. Applicants must have studied Mathematics as a main subject for at least 3 years/6 semesters, Physics for at least 1 year/2 semesters, and one of Chemistry/Electronics/Computer Science/Statistics for at least 1 year/2 semesters. Candidates with B.Sc (Hons.) in Physics or Chemistry are not eligible for this post.

TGT (Science) - To Teach Chemistry and Biology

The qualification pattern mirrors TGT (Maths): a four-year integrated degree or a Bachelor's/Honours degree (50% marks) with Chemistry, plus a B.Ed degree, along with a qualifying CTET Paper-II score. Candidates must have studied Biology/Life Science/Botany/Zoology as a Honours or main subject for at least 3 years/6 semesters, combined with Chemistry, Botany, or Zoology as applicable for at least one year or two semesters.

TGT - Work Experience Teacher (WET)

This post requires a Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or Electronics & Communication Engineering with at least 50% marks, along with a B.Ed degree (50% marks) from an NCTE-recognised institution, ability to teach in Hindi and English, and knowledge of computers. One year of practical workshop/factory experience is desirable but not mandatory.

TGT (Telugu)

Candidates need a Bachelor's degree with Telugu as the main subject (or one of three equal optional subjects), a BOL in Telugu, or a Postgraduate degree in Telugu, combined with a B.Ed with Telugu methodology or Telugu Pandit Training. Candidates must have passed State TET or CTET Paper-II with Telugu as one of the chosen subjects.

Primary Teacher

Eligible candidates need Senior Secondary/Intermediate (10+2) with 50% marks plus a 2-year Diploma in Elementary Education, OR Class XII with 50% marks plus a 4-year B.El.Ed, OR Class XII with 50% marks plus a 2-year RCI Diploma in Special Education. A qualifying score in CTET Paper-I and the ability to teach in Hindi and English are also required.

Across all posts, Hindi working knowledge is necessary, and candidates claiming equivalent qualifications must produce documentary evidence at the time of the Skill Test.

Ex-Servicemen and Central Government employees get relaxation as per Government of India orders. All concessions are concurrent, not cumulative - only the highest single permissible relaxation applies, and PwBD women do not get an additional age concession under the women's category.

SDSC SHAR Teacher Recruitment 2026 - Application Fee and Refund Rules

Here's what candidates need to pay and when they can expect a refund, since SDSC SHAR follows a two-part fee structure unlike a flat one-time fee.

Component Amount
Application Fee Rs. 250
Processing Fee Rs. 500
Total Payable at Submission Rs. 750

All candidates pay Rs. 750 online at the time of application submission, since no other payment mode is accepted. Refunds are processed only for candidates who appear in the Written Test: women, SC, ST, PwBD, and Ex-Servicemen candidates (who are exempt from the application fee) get the full Rs. 750 back, while all other candidates get Rs. 500 back after the application fee is deducted. SDSC SHAR is not responsible for pending or failed transactions, so candidates are advised to register and pay well before the closing date.

Documents Required for Online Upload

Applications without the correct uploads are rejected outright, so candidates should keep these documents scanned and ready before starting the form.

  • Recent passport-size colour photograph - JPG format, 110 x 140 pixels, under 40 KB.
  • Signature - JPG format, 200 x 50 pixels, under 20 KB.
  • SC/ST/Disability/Ex-Servicemen certificate (as applicable) - PDF, under 1 MB.
  • Essential qualification documents - PDF, under 1 MB.
  • No Objection Certificate (if employed in Government/PSU/Autonomous body).

The photograph and signature uploaded must be clear and legible; failure to meet this requirement leads to cancellation of candidature. Uploaded documents are verified at the Skill Test stage, and mere admission to the Written Test does not guarantee selection.

Selection Process: Written Test and Skill Test

SDSC SHAR shortlists and selects teachers through a two-stage process - a written exam followed by a practical skill demonstration - explained below with the exact marking scheme.

Written Test (CBT)

The Computer Based Test checks both the theoretical and practical knowledge of candidates across the prescribed syllabus. For Primary Teacher, TGT (Maths), TGT (Science), and TGT (WET), the paper carries 180 marks split into four parts - Languages (20), General Awareness/Reasoning/Computers (20), Education & Leadership Perspective (40), and Subject Specific (100). For TGT (Telugu), the 180-mark paper covers General English/Awareness/Reasoning (20), Education Perspectives (20), Pedagogy (40), and Telugu Language & Literature (100).

Post Subject-Wise Question Split Minimum Qualifying Marks
TGT (Maths) 50% Maths + 50% Physics 40% each subject; 50% aggregate
TGT (Science) 40% Biology + 30% Chemistry + 30% Physics 40% each subject; 50% aggregate

Based on Written Test performance, candidates are shortlisted for the Skill Test, generally in a 1:5 ratio with a minimum of 10 candidates category-wise.

Skill Test

The Skill Test is purely qualifying in nature, evaluated out of 100 marks, with a minimum qualifying score of 60%. It is a chalk-and-board based test where each candidate is given a subject-related topic and must demonstrate subject knowledge and teaching ability by conducting a mock class.

Final Merit and Tie-Breakers

Final selection is based purely on Written Test marks among candidates who clear the Skill Test, with empanelment done as per the number of notified vacancies. In case of a tie, the academic score of the essential qualification (PG/Graduation/Senior Secondary, as applicable) is the first tie-breaker, followed by the candidate's age (senior candidates get preference) as the second tie-breaker.

Online Registration Closes 07 July 2026, 23:59 Hrs

How to Apply Online

SDSC SHAR accepts applications exclusively through its online portal. The steps below summarise the process candidates need to follow.

  1. Visit the official SDSC SHAR website: www.shar.gov.in.
  2. Locate the online registration link for Advertisement No. SDSC SHAR/RMT/01/2026.
  3. Register and fill in the application form for the desired post code.
  4. Upload the photograph, signature, and required certificates in the specified format and size.
  5. Pay the Rs. 750 fee online (no other payment mode is accepted).
  6. Submit the application and download the registration confirmation form for future reference.

A separate application and separate fee payment is mandatory for each post; candidates cannot submit multiple applications for the same post, and incomplete applications will not be entertained.

Travelling Allowance and Other Conditions

This section covers travel reimbursement rules and a few compliance conditions candidates should be aware of before applying.

  • No Travelling Allowance is paid for attending the Written Test.
  • Outstation candidates called for the Skill Test get 2nd Class Railway Fare or normal bus fare (whichever is lower) by the shortest route, on production of journey proof.
  • Employed candidates from Central/State Government, PSUs, or Autonomous Bodies must submit a No Objection Certificate at the Skill Test/Interview stage, failing which their candidature is cancelled.
  • Only Indian Nationals can apply, and canvassing in any form leads to disqualification.
  • Selected candidates are governed by the New Defined Contribution Pension Scheme and are entitled to ISRO employee benefits including medical facilities, canteen, free transport, housing facility, LTC, group insurance, and various advances.
  • Present posting is at SDSC SHAR, Sriharikota, but selected candidates can be transferred to any ISRO/Department of Space centre in India.

Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 – FAQ's

How to apply for Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 online?

Visit your state's official WCD / ICDS portal (link provided in table above). Register with mobile & Aadhaar, fill the application form, upload documents (photo, 10th certificate, Aadhaar, domicile), and submit before the last date. Print the application acknowledgement slip after submission.

What is the eligibility for Anganwadi Worker 2026?

Candidates must have passed 10th or 12th standard from a recognized board. Age limit is 18–35 years (varies by state). Must be a permanent resident of the ward/village for which vacancy exists. Only female candidates are eligible for Worker and Helper posts.

What is the salary of Anganwadi Worker in 2026?

Anganwadi Worker receives a monthly honorarium of ₹10,000–₹20,000 depending on the state (Karnataka and TN are highest at ~₹14,000). Anganwadi Helper gets ₹5,000–₹7,000/month. The Central Government pays ₹4,500/month as base honorarium, and states add their own component on top.

Is there a written exam for Anganwadi jobs?

No, there is no written examination for Anganwadi Worker and Anganwadi Helper posts. Selection is purely merit-based on academic qualification marks (10th / 12th percentage). For Supervisor / CDPO posts, a written exam or interview may be conducted depending on the state.

What is the age limit for Anganwadi Helper?

Age limit is 18 to 35 years as of 1st January 2026 in most states. SC/ST candidates get 5 years relaxation (maximum age 40). OBC candidates get 3 years relaxation (maximum age 38). PwD candidates get additional relaxation as per state rules.

What documents are required for Anganwadi job application?

Required documents: Aadhaar card, 10th/12th marksheet and certificate, domicile/residence certificate, caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC), passport-size photograph, scanned signature, and EWS/PwD certificate if applicable. Graduation certificate is needed for Supervisor post applications.

What is ICDS recruitment 2026?

ICDS stands for Integrated Child Development Services - the government programme under which Anganwadi centres operate nationwide. ICDS recruitment 2026 refers to hiring of Anganwadi Workers, Helpers, Supervisors, and CDPOs by state WCD departments under the Ministry of Women & Child Development (wcd.nic.in).

Is Anganwadi Worker a permanent government job?

Anganwadi Workers and Helpers are honorary workers, not regular government employees. They receive a fixed monthly honorarium (not salary) and are entitled to benefits like ESI, health insurance, and maternity benefits. Supervisors and CDPOs are regular government employees in most states and receive full pay & grade pay.

Can I apply for Anganwadi job from a different district?

No. Anganwadi Workers and Helpers must be permanent residents of the same ward/village/district where the vacancy exists. A domicile or residence certificate is mandatory. Applications from outside the specified locality are rejected. For Supervisor/CDPO posts, the same district residency rule generally applies.

Eligibility for Forest Department Jobs

Eligibility for forest department jobs depends on the post, state and recruitment authority. Below is a general idea of qualification and age for popular posts like Forest Guard, Forester and Forest Range Officer. Candidates should always check the official notification for detailed eligibility criteria.

Education Qualification for Forest Guard, Forester, Ranger

  • Forest Guard / Field Guard / Forest Watcher / Beat Guard: Usually 10th pass or 12th pass from a recognized board, knowledge of local language, and basic physical standards as per state rules.
  • Forester / Section Forest Officer / Deputy Forest Ranger: Generally 12th pass or graduate in any stream or science-related subjects, with physical standards and sometimes driving or technical skills depending on the post.
  • Forest Range Officer (RFO) / Forest Ranger / ACF: Normally graduate degree in Science, Agriculture, Forestry, Environmental Science, Engineering or related disciplines, with higher physical standards and sometimes a competitive exam similar to state PCS level.
  • IFS / Indian Forest Service and senior posts (DCF, CF, CCF, PCCF): Filled through UPSC Indian Forest Service Examination and promotions, requiring a graduate degree and all-India competitive selection.

Age Limit & Relaxation

  • Forest Guard / Forester / Field Guard: Minimum age is usually 18 years and maximum age is around 27–30 years, with age relaxation for SC, ST, OBC, EWS, Ex-servicemen and other categories as per government rules.
  • Forest Range Officer / ACF and higher competitive posts: Age limit often ranges from 21 to 32 years (varies by recruitment), with relaxations for reserved categories.
  • Exact age limit, cut-off date and relaxation details always depend on the particular notification, so candidates should verify from the official advertisement before applying.
